1	"""Record punches from punch_stream.ino and reconstruct their paths in 3D.
2	
3	Install:  pip install numpy matplotlib pyserial
4	
5	Record:   python punch_tracker.py capture --port COM5 --seconds 30 --out punches.csv
6	Analyse:  python punch_tracker.py analyze punches.csv
7	          python punch_tracker.py analyze punches.csv --save punches.png
8	Live:     python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7 --dry-run
9	          python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7
10	
11	Live mode (Windows only) presses w for a straight punch and s for a punch that
12	also travels up or down, such as an uppercut or body shot. Keys go to whichever
13	window has focus, so use --dry-run to see the angles and tune --angle first.
14	Hold still for 2 s at the start, and pause briefly before each punch. Stop with
15	Ctrl+C.
16	
17	While recording, hold still for the first 2 seconds, then rest for at least
18	1 second before and after each punch. Rest periods are what stop the error from
19	growing, so back-to-back combinations cannot be reconstructed.
20	
21	Paths are rough estimates: compare shape and direction between punches rather
22	than trusting exact distances. "Forward" is the direction of the punch's furthest
23	point, because the sensor cannot measure compass heading.
24	"""
25	
26	import argparse
27	import csv
28	import struct
29	import sys
30	import time
31	from collections import deque
32	from dataclasses import dataclass
33	
34	import numpy as np
35	
36	# Must match the sensor settings in punch_stream.ino
37	ACCEL_LSB_PER_G = 2048.0
38	GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS = 16.4
39	FRAME_SIZE = 19
40	SYNC = b"\xa5\x5a"
41	
42	CLIP_RAW = 32700  # raw readings beyond this are treated as saturated
43	GRAVITY = 9.80665
44	
45	# Detection settings: tune these against your own recordings
46	STILL_ACCEL_G = 0.15  # still means acceleration within this of 1 g
47	STILL_GYRO_DPS = 30.0  # and rotation below this
48	STILL_WINDOW_S = 0.15  # for at least this long
49	PUNCH_THRESHOLD_G = 2.0  # a motion is a punch if total acceleration deviates this far from 1 g
50	MAX_PUNCH_S = 2.0  # longer motions are skipped, because drift gets too large
51	CALIBRATION_MIN_S = 1.0
52	GRAVITY_WINDOW_S = 0.1  # rest period before a punch used to find "down"
53	
54	# Live detection settings: tune these with --dry-run
55	TWO_DIRECTION_ANGLE_DEG = 35.0  # punches this far above or below level press s instead of w
56	MIN_PUNCH_SPEED_MS = 1.0  # slower motions are ignored, even with a hard jolt
57	SPEED_DROP_RATIO = 0.8  # the peak has passed once speed falls to this fraction of it
58	MAX_DECISION_S = 0.4  # give up this long after the threshold if no peak was found
59	MAX_FRAME_GAP_S = 0.05  # a longer gap in the data means the sensor state is unknown
60	NOT_READY_REPORT_S = 3.0  # say why punches are not being detected after this long
61	NO_DATA_REPORT_S = 2.0
62	KEY_HOLD_S = 0.05
63	STRAIGHT_KEY = "w"
64	TWO_DIRECTION_KEY = "s"
65	SCAN_CODES = {"w": 0x11, "s": 0x1F}  # physical key codes, which games also recognise
66	
67	MAX_PLOTTED_PUNCHES = 8
68	PUNCH_COLORS = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100",
69	                "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#6250d6", "#e34948"]
70	SURFACE = "#fcfcfb"
71	TEXT_PRIMARY = "#0b0b0b"
72	TEXT_SECONDARY = "#52514e"
73	GRID = "#e4e3df"
74	
75	
76	@dataclass
77	class Punch:
78	    number: int
79	    start_s: float
80	    duration_s: float
81	    peak_g: float
82	    peak_gyro_dps: float
83	    reach_m: float
84	    peak_speed_ms: float
85	    end_speed_error_ms: float  # NaN when the path was cut short by clipping
86	    clipped_samples: int
87	    gap_samples: int
88	    time_s: np.ndarray
89	    position_m: np.ndarray  # columns: forward, sideways, up
90	
91	
92	def parse_frames(buffer):
93	    """Return complete valid frames from buffer and the bytes left unparsed."""
94	    frames = []
95	    position = 0
96	    while True:
97	        position = buffer.find(SYNC, position)
98	        if position < 0:
99	            # Keep a trailing first sync byte, in case the second is still arriving
100	            return frames, buffer[-1:] if buffer[-1:] == SYNC[:1] else bytearray()
101	        if position + FRAME_SIZE > len(buffer):
102	            return frames, buffer[position:]
103	
104	        payload = buffer[position + 2:position + 18]
105	        checksum = 0
106	        for byte in payload:
107	            checksum ^= byte
108	        if checksum != buffer[position + 18]:
109	            position += 1
110	            continue
111	
112	        timestamp = struct.unpack("<I", payload[:4])[0]
113	        frames.append((timestamp, *struct.unpack(">6h", payload[4:])))
114	        position += FRAME_SIZE
115	
116	
117	def capture(port, baud, seconds, out_path):
118	    import serial
119	
120	    with serial.Serial(port, baud, timeout=0.1) as connection, \
121	            open(out_path, "w", newline="") as out_file:
122	        writer = csv.writer(out_file)
123	        writer.writerow(["t_us", "ax", "ay", "az", "gx", "gy", "gz"])
124	
125	        print("Connecting (the Uno resets when the port opens)...")
126	        connect_deadline = time.monotonic() + 5.0
127	        buffer = bytearray()
128	        all_frames = []
129	        recording_until = None
130	
131	        while recording_until is None or time.monotonic() < recording_until:
132	            buffer += connection.read(4096)
133	            frames, buffer = parse_frames(buffer)
134	            if frames:
135	                writer.writerows(frames)
136	                all_frames.extend(frames)
137	                if recording_until is None:
138	                    recording_until = time.monotonic() + seconds
139	                    print(f"Recording for {seconds:g} s. "
140	                          "Hold still for 2 s, then start punching.")
141	            elif recording_until is None and time.monotonic() > connect_deadline:
142	                text = bytes(buffer).decode("ascii", "replace").strip()
143	                sys.exit("No data received. Check the port and baud rate, that "
144	                         "punch_stream.ino is uploaded, and that the Serial "
145	                         f"Monitor is closed. Received: {text[:100]!r}")
146	
147	    data = np.array(all_frames, dtype=np.int64)
148	    t = np.unwrap(data[:, 0].astype(float), period=2.0**32) / 1e6
149	    gaps = np.diff(t)
150	    print(f"Saved {len(data)} samples to {out_path} "
151	          f"({1 / np.median(gaps):.0f} Hz).")
152	    print(f"Timing gaps: {int(np.sum(gaps > 1.5 * np.median(gaps)))}")
153	    print(f"Clipped accel samples: {int(np.sum(np.abs(data[:, 1:4]).max(axis=1) >= CLIP_RAW))}")
154	    print(f"Clipped gyro samples: {int(np.sum(np.abs(data[:, 4:7]).max(axis=1) >= CLIP_RAW))}")
155	
156	
157	def load_recording(path):
158	    data = np.loadtxt(path, delimiter=",", skiprows=1, ndmin=2)
159	    if len(data) < 2:
160	        sys.exit(f"{path} does not contain enough samples.")
161	    t = np.unwrap(data[:, 0], period=2.0**32) / 1e6
162	    return t - t[0], data[:, 1:4], data[:, 4:7]
163	
164	
165	def find_still(t, accel_g, gyro_dps):
166	    rate = 1.0 / np.median(np.diff(t))
167	    window = max(1, int(STILL_WINDOW_S * rate)) | 1
168	    accel_excess = np.abs(np.linalg.norm(accel_g, axis=1) - 1.0)
169	    instant = (accel_excess < STILL_ACCEL_G) & (np.linalg.norm(gyro_dps, axis=1) < STILL_GYRO_DPS)
170	    return np.convolve(instant.astype(int), np.ones(window, dtype=int), "same") == window
171	
172	
173	def runs_of(mask):
174	    """Return (start, end) index pairs for each run of True, with end exclusive."""
175	    edges = np.diff(np.concatenate(([0], mask.astype(int), [0])))
176	    return list(zip(np.flatnonzero(edges == 1), np.flatnonzero(edges == -1)))
177	
178	
179	def quat_multiply(a, b):
180	    aw, ax, ay, az = a
181	    bw, bx, by, bz = b
182	    return np.array([aw * bw - ax * bx - ay * by - az * bz,
183	                     aw * bx + ax * bw + ay * bz - az * by,
184	                     aw * by - ax * bz + ay * bw + az * bx,
185	                     aw * bz + ax * by - ay * bx + az * bw])
186	
187	
188	def quat_rotate(q, v):
189	    u = q[1:]
190	    return v + 2.0 * np.cross(u, np.cross(u, v) + q[0] * v)
191	
192	
193	def quat_to_world_up(specific_force):
194	    """Return the rotation taking the at-rest accelerometer reading to world +Z."""
195	    f = specific_force / np.linalg.norm(specific_force)
196	    if f[2] < -0.999999:
197	        return np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
198	    q = np.array([1.0 + f[2], f[1], -f[0], 0.0])
199	    return q / np.linalg.norm(q)
200	
201	
202	def quat_step(q, mean_rate, dt):
203	    """Advance orientation q by a body rotation rate (rad/s) held for dt seconds."""
204	    half_angle = 0.5 * np.linalg.norm(mean_rate) * dt
205	    axis = mean_rate / np.linalg.norm(mean_rate) if half_angle > 0 else mean_rate
206	    q = quat_multiply(q, np.concatenate(([np.cos(half_angle)], np.sin(half_angle) * axis)))
207	    return q / np.linalg.norm(q)
208	
209	
210	def cumulative_trapezoid(values, t):
211	    steps = 0.5 * (values[1:] + values[:-1]) * np.diff(t)[:, None]
212	    return np.vstack((np.zeros(values.shape[1]), np.cumsum(steps, axis=0)))
213	
214	
215	def reconstruct(number, t, accel_raw, gyro_raw, gyro_bias_dps, start, end):
216	    accel_ms2 = accel_raw / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * GRAVITY
217	    gyro_rad = np.radians(gyro_raw / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS - gyro_bias_dps)
218	
219	    rate = 1.0 / np.median(np.diff(t))
220	    gravity_samples = max(1, int(GRAVITY_WINDOW_S * rate))
221	    specific_force = accel_ms2[max(0, start - gravity_samples):start].mean(axis=0)
222	    gravity_world = np.array([0.0, 0.0, np.linalg.norm(specific_force)])
223	
224	    saturated = (np.abs(accel_raw[start:end]).max(axis=1) >= CLIP_RAW) | \
225	                (np.abs(gyro_raw[start:end]).max(axis=1) >= CLIP_RAW)
226	    clipped_samples = int(saturated.sum())
227	    # Clipped readings are wrong by an unknown amount, so the path stops there
228	    stop = start + int(np.argmax(saturated)) if clipped_samples else end
229	    if stop - start < 3:
230	        return None
231	
232	    q = quat_to_world_up(specific_force)
233	    linear_world = np.zeros((stop - start, 3))
234	    for k in range(stop - start):
235	        i = start + k
236	        if k:
237	            q = quat_step(q, 0.5 * (gyro_rad[i - 1] + gyro_rad[i]), t[i] - t[i - 1])
238	        linear_world[k] = quat_rotate(q, accel_ms2[i]) - gravity_world
239	
240	    time_s = t[start:stop] - t[start]
241	    velocity = cumulative_trapezoid(linear_world, time_s)
242	    end_speed_error = float("nan")
243	    if not clipped_samples:
244	        # The glove is at rest at both ends, so any leftover velocity is accumulated error
245	        end_speed_error = float(np.linalg.norm(velocity[-1]))
246	        velocity -= np.outer(time_s / time_s[-1], velocity[-1])
247	
248	    position = cumulative_trapezoid(velocity, time_s)
249	    distances = np.linalg.norm(position, axis=1)
250	    furthest = position[int(np.argmax(distances))]
251	    heading = np.arctan2(furthest[1], furthest[0])
252	    cos_h, sin_h = np.cos(-heading), np.sin(-heading)
253	    aligned = np.column_stack((cos_h * position[:, 0] - sin_h * position[:, 1],
254	                               sin_h * position[:, 0] + cos_h * position[:, 1],
255	                               position[:, 2]))
256	
257	    dt = np.diff(t[start:stop])
258	    return Punch(
259	        number=number,
260	        start_s=float(t[start]),
261	        duration_s=float(t[stop - 1] - t[start]),
262	        peak_g=float(np.max(np.abs(np.linalg.norm(accel_raw[start:end], axis=1) / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G - 1.0))),
263	        peak_gyro_dps=float(np.max(np.linalg.norm(gyro_raw[start:end], axis=1) / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS)),
264	        reach_m=float(distances.max()),
265	        peak_speed_ms=float(np.linalg.norm(velocity, axis=1).max()),
266	        end_speed_error_ms=end_speed_error,
267	        clipped_samples=clipped_samples,
268	        gap_samples=int(np.sum(dt > 1.5 / rate)),
269	        time_s=time_s,
270	        position_m=aligned,
271	    )
272	
273	
274	def find_punches(t, accel_raw, gyro_raw):
275	    accel_g = accel_raw / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G
276	    gyro_dps = gyro_raw / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS
277	    still = find_still(t, accel_g, gyro_dps)
278	
279	    calibration = next(((a, b) for a, b in runs_of(still)
280	                        if t[b - 1] - t[a] >= CALIBRATION_MIN_S), None)
281	    if calibration is None:
282	        sys.exit(f"No still period of at least {CALIBRATION_MIN_S:g} s found. "
283	                 "Hold the glove still for 2 s at the start of the recording.")
284	    gyro_bias_dps = gyro_dps[calibration[0]:calibration[1]].mean(axis=0)
285	
286	    punches = []
287	    accel_excess = np.abs(np.linalg.norm(accel_g, axis=1) - 1.0)
288	    for start, end in runs_of(~still):
289	        if accel_excess[start:end].max() < PUNCH_THRESHOLD_G:
290	            continue
291	        if start == 0 or end == len(t):
292	            print(f"Skipped motion at {t[start]:.2f} s: recording starts or ends during it.")
293	            continue
294	        if t[end - 1] - t[start] > MAX_PUNCH_S:
295	            print(f"Skipped motion at {t[start]:.2f} s: lasted over {MAX_PUNCH_S:g} s without a rest.")
296	            continue
297	        punch = reconstruct(len(punches) + 1, t, accel_raw, gyro_raw, gyro_bias_dps, start, end)
298	        if punch is None:
299	            print(f"Skipped motion at {t[start]:.2f} s: sensor clipped almost immediately.")
300	            continue
301	        punches.append(punch)
302	    return punches
303	
304	
305	def print_report(punches):
306	    if not punches:
307	        print(f"No punches found. Nothing exceeded {PUNCH_THRESHOLD_G:g} g between rest periods.")
308	        return
309	
310	    print(f"{'#':>2} {'start s':>8} {'length s':>8} {'peak g':>7} {'gyro d/s':>8} "
311	          f"{'reach m':>8} {'speed m/s':>9} {'end err m/s':>11}  notes")
312	    for p in punches:
313	        notes = []
314	        if p.clipped_samples:
315	            notes.append(f"CLIPPED, path stops at first of {p.clipped_samples} clipped samples")
316	        if p.gap_samples:
317	            notes.append(f"{p.gap_samples} timing gaps")
318	        error = "n/a" if np.isnan(p.end_speed_error_ms) else f"{p.end_speed_error_ms:.2f}"
319	        print(f"{p.number:>2} {p.start_s:>8.2f} {p.duration_s:>8.2f} {p.peak_g:>7.1f} "
320	              f"{p.peak_gyro_dps:>8.0f} {p.reach_m:>8.2f} {p.peak_speed_ms:>9.2f} {error:>11}  "
321	              f"{'; '.join(notes)}")
322	    print("\n'end err' is the leftover speed when the glove stopped, which should be 0. "
323	          "The larger it is, the less reliable that path is.")
324	
325	
326	def plot(t, accel_raw, punches, save_path):
327	    import matplotlib
328	    if save_path:
329	        matplotlib.use("Agg")
330	    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
331	
332	    if len(punches) > MAX_PLOTTED_PUNCHES:
333	        print(f"Plotting the first {MAX_PLOTTED_PUNCHES} punches. "
334	              "The table above includes all of them.")
335	    shown = punches[:MAX_PLOTTED_PUNCHES]
336	
337	    plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 10, "text.color": TEXT_PRIMARY,
338	                         "axes.labelcolor": TEXT_SECONDARY,
339	                         "xtick.color": TEXT_SECONDARY, "ytick.color": TEXT_SECONDARY})
340	    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(13, 5.5), facecolor=SURFACE)
341	
342	    path_ax = fig.add_subplot(1, 2, 1, projection="3d", facecolor=SURFACE)
343	    for i, p in enumerate(shown):
344	        x, y, z = p.position_m.T
345	        path_ax.plot(x, y, z, color=PUNCH_COLORS[i], linewidth=2, label=f"Punch {p.number}")
346	        path_ax.scatter(x[-1], y[-1], z[-1], color=PUNCH_COLORS[i], s=30, depthshade=False)
347	
348	    all_points = np.vstack([p.position_m for p in shown] + [np.zeros((1, 3))])
349	    center = 0.5 * (all_points.max(axis=0) + all_points.min(axis=0))
350	    half_range = max(0.5 * (all_points.max(axis=0) - all_points.min(axis=0)).max(), 0.01)
351	    path_ax.set_xlim(center[0] - half_range, center[0] + half_range)
352	    path_ax.set_ylim(center[1] - half_range, center[1] + half_range)
353	    path_ax.set_zlim(center[2] - half_range, center[2] + half_range)
354	    path_ax.set_box_aspect((1, 1, 1))
355	    path_ax.set_xlabel("Forward (m)")
356	    path_ax.set_ylabel("Sideways (m)")
357	    path_ax.set_zlabel("Up (m)")
358	    for axis in (path_ax.xaxis, path_ax.yaxis, path_ax.zaxis):
359	        axis.set_pane_color((1, 1, 1, 0))
360	        axis._axinfo["grid"]["color"] = GRID
361	    path_ax.set_title("Punch paths, each starting at 0, 0, 0", loc="left", fontsize=12)
362	    if len(shown) >= 2:
363	        path_ax.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=False, labelcolor=TEXT_SECONDARY)
364	
365	    time_ax = fig.add_subplot(1, 2, 2, facecolor=SURFACE)
366	    magnitude = np.linalg.norm(accel_raw, axis=1) / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G
367	    time_ax.plot(t, magnitude, color=TEXT_SECONDARY, linewidth=1)
368	    top = max(magnitude.max() * 1.1, 2.0)
369	    time_ax.set_ylim(0, top)
370	    time_ax.set_xlim(t[0], t[-1])
371	    for i, p in enumerate(shown):
372	        time_ax.axvspan(p.start_s, p.start_s + p.duration_s, color=PUNCH_COLORS[i], alpha=0.25, linewidth=0)
373	        time_ax.text(p.start_s + p.duration_s / 2, top * 0.97, str(p.number),
374	                     ha="center", va="top", color=TEXT_PRIMARY)
375	    time_ax.set_xlabel("Time (s)")
376	    time_ax.set_ylabel("Acceleration magnitude (g)")
377	    time_ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, linewidth=0.8)
378	    time_ax.set_axisbelow(True)
379	    for side in ("top", "right"):
380	        time_ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
381	    for side in ("left", "bottom"):
382	        time_ax.spines[side].set_color(GRID)
383	    time_ax.set_title("Detected punches in the recording", loc="left", fontsize=12)
384	
385	    fig.tight_layout()
386	    if save_path:
387	        fig.savefig(save_path, dpi=150, facecolor=SURFACE)
388	        print(f"Saved plot to {save_path}")
389	    else:
390	        plt.show()
391	
392	
393	@dataclass
394	class LivePunch:
395	    key: str
396	    angle_deg: float  # above (+) or below (-) level, at peak speed
397	    speed_ms: float
398	    reaction_s: float  # from the start of the motion to this decision
399	
400	
401	class LiveDetector:
402	    """Classify punches one sample at a time, as soon as they pass peak speed.
403	
404	    Direction is read at peak speed rather than when the glove stops, because that
405	    is both sooner and more accurate: error has had less time to grow, and the
406	    retraction has not started.
407	    """
408	
409	    CALIBRATING, WAITING, READY, TRACKING = range(4)
410	
411	    def __init__(self, angle_deg=TWO_DIRECTION_ANGLE_DEG):
412	        self.angle_deg = angle_deg
413	        self.state = self.CALIBRATING
414	        self.gyro_bias_dps = None
415	        self.last_us = None
416	        self._reset_rest()
417	        self._reset_not_ready()
418	
419	    def _reset_not_ready(self):
420	        self.not_ready_s = 0.0
421	        self.not_ready_accel_g = 0.0
422	        self.not_ready_gyro_dps = 0.0
423	        self.not_ready_count = 0
424	
425	    def _report_not_ready(self, dt, accel_g, gyro_dps):
426	        """Explain a long wait for rest, which would otherwise look like a silent hang."""
427	        if self.state not in (self.CALIBRATING, self.WAITING):
428	            self._reset_not_ready()
429	            return
430	        self.not_ready_s += dt
431	        self.not_ready_accel_g += accel_g
432	        self.not_ready_gyro_dps += gyro_dps
433	        self.not_ready_count += 1
434	        if self.not_ready_s < NOT_READY_REPORT_S:
435	            return
436	        accel = self.not_ready_accel_g / self.not_ready_count
437	        gyro = self.not_ready_gyro_dps / self.not_ready_count
438	        hint = ("The sensor looks like it reset, so check its wiring."
439	                if accel < 0.5 or accel > 2.0 else "Hold still briefly to re-arm.")
440	        print(f"Not ready: average accel {accel:.2f} g (needs about 1), average rotation "
441	              f"{gyro:.0f} deg/s (needs under {STILL_GYRO_DPS:g}). {hint}")
442	        self._reset_not_ready()
443	
444	    def _reset_rest(self):
445	        self.still_s = 0.0
446	        self.rest_accel = deque()  # (seconds since rest began, accel) for finding "down"
447	        self.gyro_sum = np.zeros(3)
448	        self.gyro_count = 0
449	
450	    def feed(self, frame):
451	        """Process one (t_us, ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz) frame. Returns a LivePunch or None."""
452	        # Timestamps are uint32 microseconds, which wrap every 71 minutes
453	        dt = 0.0 if self.last_us is None else ((frame[0] - self.last_us) & 0xFFFFFFFF) / 1e6
454	        self.last_us = frame[0]
455	        if dt > MAX_FRAME_GAP_S:
456	            self._reset_rest()
457	            self.state = self.CALIBRATING if self.gyro_bias_dps is None else self.WAITING
458	            return None
459	
460	        accel_raw = np.array(frame[1:4], dtype=float)
461	        gyro_raw = np.array(frame[4:7], dtype=float)
462	        accel_g = np.linalg.norm(accel_raw) / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G
463	        accel_excess = abs(accel_g - 1.0)
464	        gyro_dps = gyro_raw / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS
465	        still = accel_excess < STILL_ACCEL_G and np.linalg.norm(gyro_dps) < STILL_GYRO_DPS
466	        self._report_not_ready(dt, accel_g, np.linalg.norm(gyro_dps))
467	
468	        if self.state == self.READY and not still:
469	            self._begin_tracking(accel_raw, gyro_dps)
470	
471	        if still:
472	            self.still_s += dt
473	            self.rest_accel.append((self.still_s, accel_raw))
474	            while self.rest_accel[0][0] < self.still_s - GRAVITY_WINDOW_S:
475	                self.rest_accel.popleft()
476	            self.gyro_sum += gyro_dps
477	            self.gyro_count += 1
478	        else:
479	            self._reset_rest()
480	
481	        if self.state == self.CALIBRATING:
482	            if self.still_s >= CALIBRATION_MIN_S:
483	                self.gyro_bias_dps = self.gyro_sum / self.gyro_count
484	                self.state = self.READY
485	                print("Ready. Pause briefly before each punch.")
486	        elif self.state == self.WAITING:
487	            if self.still_s >= STILL_WINDOW_S:
488	                self.state = self.READY
489	        elif self.state == self.TRACKING and dt > 0:
490	            return self._track(dt, accel_raw, gyro_raw, gyro_dps, accel_excess)
491	        return None
492	
493	    def _begin_tracking(self, accel_raw, gyro_dps):
494	        rest_force = np.mean([a for _, a in self.rest_accel], axis=0) / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * GRAVITY
495	        self.gravity_world = np.array([0.0, 0.0, np.linalg.norm(rest_force)])
496	        self.q = quat_to_world_up(rest_force)
497	        self.prev_rate = np.radians(gyro_dps - self.gyro_bias_dps)
498	        self.prev_linear = quat_rotate(self.q, accel_raw / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * GRAVITY) - self.gravity_world
499	        self.velocity = np.zeros(3)
500	        self.peak_velocity = np.zeros(3)
501	        self.peak_speed = 0.0
502	        self.elapsed_s = 0.0
503	        self.armed_at_s = None
504	        self.state = self.TRACKING
505	
506	    def _track(self, dt, accel_raw, gyro_raw, gyro_dps, accel_excess):
507	        self.elapsed_s += dt
508	        if self.armed_at_s is None and accel_excess >= PUNCH_THRESHOLD_G:
509	            self.armed_at_s = self.elapsed_s
510	        clipped = max(np.abs(accel_raw).max(), np.abs(gyro_raw).max()) >= CLIP_RAW
511	
512	        if not clipped:  # clipped readings are wrong by an unknown amount
513	            rate = np.radians(gyro_dps - self.gyro_bias_dps)
514	            self.q = quat_step(self.q, 0.5 * (self.prev_rate + rate), dt)
515	            linear = quat_rotate(self.q, accel_raw / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * GRAVITY) - self.gravity_world
516	            self.velocity = self.velocity + 0.5 * (self.prev_linear + linear) * dt
517	            self.prev_rate, self.prev_linear = rate, linear
518	            speed = np.linalg.norm(self.velocity)
519	            if speed > self.peak_speed:
520	                self.peak_speed = speed
521	                self.peak_velocity = self.velocity
522	
523	        if self.armed_at_s is None:
524	            if self.still_s >= STILL_WINDOW_S:
525	                self.state = self.READY  # just a small movement, not a punch
526	            elif self.elapsed_s > MAX_PUNCH_S:
527	                self.state = self.WAITING
528	            return None
529	
530	        fast_enough = self.peak_speed >= MIN_PUNCH_SPEED_MS
531	        past_peak = fast_enough and np.linalg.norm(self.velocity) < SPEED_DROP_RATIO * self.peak_speed
532	        timed_out = self.elapsed_s - self.armed_at_s >= MAX_DECISION_S
533	        if not (clipped or past_peak or timed_out):
534	            return None
535	
536	        self.state = self.WAITING
537	        if not fast_enough:
538	            return None
539	        vx, vy, vz = self.peak_velocity
540	        angle = float(np.degrees(np.arctan2(vz, np.hypot(vx, vy))))
541	        key = TWO_DIRECTION_KEY if abs(angle) >= self.angle_deg else STRAIGHT_KEY
542	        return LivePunch(key, angle, float(self.peak_speed), self.elapsed_s)
543

545	def press_key(key):
546	    """Tap a key using Windows SendInput. Returns False if Windows rejected it."""
547	    import ctypes
548	    from ctypes import wintypes
549	
550	    class KEYBDINPUT(ctypes.Structure):
551	        _fields_ = [("wVk", wintypes.WORD), ("wScan", wintypes.WORD), ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD),
552	                    ("time", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwExtraInfo", ctypes.c_size_t)]
553	
554	    class MOUSEINPUT(ctypes.Structure):  # never sent, but it sets the size of the union
555	        _fields_ = [("dx", wintypes.LONG), ("dy", wintypes.LONG), ("mouseData", wintypes.DWORD),
556	                    ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD), ("time", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwExtraInfo", ctypes.c_size_t)]
557	
558	    class INPUTUNION(ctypes.Union):
559	        _fields_ = [("ki", KEYBDINPUT), ("mi", MOUSEINPUT)]
560	
561	    class INPUT(ctypes.Structure):
562	        _fields_ = [("type", wintypes.DWORD), ("union", INPUTUNION)]
563	
564	    INPUT_KEYBOARD, KEYEVENTF_KEYUP, KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE = 1, 0x0002, 0x0008
565	
566	    def send(flags):
567	        event = INPUT(INPUT_KEYBOARD, INPUTUNION(ki=KEYBDINPUT(0, SCAN_CODES[key], flags, 0, 0)))
568	        return ctypes.windll.user32.SendInput(1, ctypes.byref(event), ctypes.sizeof(INPUT)) == 1
569	
570	    pressed = send(KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE)
571	    time.sleep(KEY_HOLD_S)
572	    return send(KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE | KEYEVENTF_KEYUP) and pressed

1	"""Receive glove IMU frames over UDP.
2	
3	Frame (19 bytes): A5 5A | uint32 us (little-endian) | ax ay az gx gy gz int16 (big-endian) | XOR of bytes 2-17
4	Run directly to print incoming data, or with --simulate to fake a glove for testing.
5	"""
6	import argparse
7	import socket
8	import struct
9	import threading
10	import time
11	from collections import deque
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	
14	import numpy as np
15	
16	PORT = 5005
17	SYNC = b"\xA5\x5A"
18	FRAME_LEN = 19
19	
20	# Must match the ranges the firmware sets on the MPU.
21	ACCEL_LSB_PER_G = 2048.0   # +-16 g; 16384 = +-2 g, 8192 = +-4 g, 4096 = +-8 g
22	GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS = 16.4    # +-2000 deg/s; 131 = +-250, 65.5 = +-500, 32.8 = +-1000
23	
24	# How the sensor sits on the glove: glove axis i = AXIS_SIGN[i] * sensor axis AXIS_MAP[i]
25	AXIS_MAP = [0, 1, 2]
26	AXIS_SIGN = np.array([1, 1, 1])
27	
28	# Frames carry no glove id, so identify the glove by its sender IP.
29	GLOVE_BY_IP = {}        # e.g. {"192.168.137.20": "L", "192.168.137.21": "R"}
30	DEFAULT_GLOVE = "L"
31	
32	
33	@dataclass
34	class Sample:
35	    t_us: int            # ESP32 clock (wraps every ~71 min)
36	    accel: np.ndarray    # g, in glove axes
37	    gyro: np.ndarray     # deg/s, in glove axes
38	    t: float = 0.0       # when it was measured, on the laptop clock (time.time()); set by Clock
39	    dt: float = 0.0      # seconds since the previous sample, from t_us; a dropped packet shows as a big dt
40	
41	
42	def checksum(body):
43	    out = 0
44	    for b in body:
45	        out ^= b
46	    return out
47	
48	
49	def parse_frames(data):
50	    """Yield a Sample for every valid frame in data; junk or corrupt bytes are skipped."""
51	    i = 0
52	    while i + FRAME_LEN <= len(data):
53	        if data[i:i + 2] == SYNC and checksum(data[i + 2:i + 18]) == data[i + 18]:
54	            (t_us,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, i + 2)
55	            raw = np.array(struct.unpack_from(">6h", data, i + 6), dtype=float)
56	            accel = raw[:3][AXIS_MAP] / ACCEL_LSB_PER_G * AXIS_SIGN
57	            gyro = raw[3:][AXIS_MAP] / GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS * AXIS_SIGN
58	            yield Sample(t_us, accel, gyro)
59	            i += FRAME_LEN
60	        else:
61	            i += 1  # resync
62	
63	
64	def pack_frame(t_us, accel, gyro):
65	    """Build a frame from accel (g) and gyro (deg/s); used by the simulator and tests."""
66	    counts = np.concatenate([np.asarray(accel) * ACCEL_LSB_PER_G, np.asarray(gyro) * GYRO_LSB_PER_DPS])
67	    body = struct.pack("<I", t_us & 0xFFFFFFFF) + struct.pack(">6h", *np.clip(np.round(counts), -32768, 32767).astype(int))
68	    return SYNC + body + bytes([checksum(body)])
69	
70	
71	class Clock:
72	    """Puts one glove's ESP32 microsecond counter on the laptop clock.
73	
74	    Packets arrive late and in bursts, so arrival time is too jittery to use directly. Instead the
75	    ESP32 time is unwrapped and shifted by the smallest (arrival - ESP32 time) seen recently, which
76	    is the packet that suffered the least delay. The result is smooth and off by only that minimum
77	    WiFi latency (a few ms).
78	    """
79	    MASK = 0xFFFFFFFF
80	    RESET_US = 5_000_000   # a step bigger than this means a reboot or long outage
81	
82	    def __init__(self, window=500):
83	        self.last_us, self.elapsed_us = None, 0
84	        self.offsets = deque(maxlen=window)
85	
86	    def stamp(self, sample, arrival):
87	        step = (sample.t_us - self.last_us) & self.MASK if self.last_us is not None else 0
88	        if self.last_us is None or step > self.RESET_US:  # first sample, reboot, or long outage
89	            self.elapsed_us, step = sample.t_us, 0
90	            self.offsets.clear()
91	        else:
92	            self.elapsed_us += step  # modular difference, so the 32-bit rollover is harmless
93	        self.last_us = sample.t_us
94	        t_esp = self.elapsed_us / 1e6
95	        self.offsets.append(arrival - t_esp)
96	        sample.dt, sample.t = step / 1e6, t_esp + min(self.offsets)
97	
98	
99	class GloveReceiver:
100	    """Background UDP listener. samples[glove_id] holds the most recent readings."""
101	
102	    def __init__(self, port=PORT, history=1000):
103	        self.sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
104	        self.sock.bind(("0.0.0.0", port))
105	        self.samples, self.clocks, self.history = {}, {}, history
106	        threading.Thread(target=self._listen, daemon=True).start()
107	
108	    def _listen(self):
109	        while True:
110	            data, addr = self.sock.recvfrom(2048)
111	            arrival = time.time()
112	            glove = GLOVE_BY_IP.get(addr[0], DEFAULT_GLOVE)
113	            clock = self.clocks.setdefault(glove, Clock())
114	            for sample in parse_frames(data):
115	                clock.stamp(sample, arrival)
116	                self.samples.setdefault(glove, deque(maxlen=self.history)).append(sample)
117	
118	    def latest(self, glove):
119	        buf = self.samples.get(glove)
120	        return buf[-1] if buf else None
121	
122	    def recent(self, glove, seconds):
123	        cutoff = time.time() - seconds
124	        return [s for s in list(self.samples.get(glove, [])) if s.t >= cutoff]
125	
126	
127	def simulate(port=PORT, hz=200):
128	    """Send fake frames: a resting glove with an 80 ms punch every 1.5 s."""
129	    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
130	    t0 = time.time()
131	    while True:
132	        t = time.time() - t0
133	        phase = t % 1.5
134	        bump = np.sin(np.pi * phase / 0.08) if phase < 0.08 else 0.0
135	        accel = np.array([8 * bump, 0, 1]) + np.random.normal(0, 0.02, 3)
136	        gyro = np.array([0, 0, 300 * bump]) + np.random.normal(0, 1, 3)
137	        sock.sendto(pack_frame(int(t * 1e6), accel, gyro), ("127.0.0.1", port))
138	        time.sleep(1 / hz)
139	
140	
141	if __name__ == "__main__":
142	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
143	    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="send fake glove data to ourselves")
144	    args = parser.parse_args()
145	
146	    receiver = GloveReceiver()
147	    if args.simulate:
148	        threading.Thread(target=simulate, daemon=True).start()
149	    while True:
150	        time.sleep(0.5)
151	        for glove in list(receiver.samples):
152	            recent = receiver.recent(glove, 0.5)
153	            peak = max((np.linalg.norm(s.accel) for s in recent), default=0)
154	            print(f"glove {glove}: {len(recent) * 2} Hz, peak accel {peak:.1f} g, gyro {receiver.latest(glove).gyro.round(0)}")

47	class Smoother:
48	    """Exponential moving average over a landmark array."""
49	
50	    def __init__(self, alpha):
51	        self.alpha, self.prev = alpha, None
52	
53	    def __call__(self, x):
54	        self.prev = x if self.prev is None else self.alpha * x + (1 - self.alpha) * self.prev
55	        return self.prev
56	
57	
58	def punch_travel(delta, start, end, world, sw):
59	    """Per hand (extension, right, up) in shoulder-widths.
60	
61	    delta = wrist movement relative to the shoulder; start/end = wrist-to-shoulder vectors.
62	    Extension is how much the arm straightened, so it needs no facing direction.
63	    """
64	    right = world[R_SH] - world[L_SH]
65	    right[1] = 0
66	    right /= np.linalg.norm(right) + 1e-6
67	    extension = (np.linalg.norm(end, axis=1) - np.linalg.norm(start, axis=1)) / sw
68	    return np.stack([extension, delta @ right, -delta[:, 1]], axis=1)
69	
70	
71	def classify_punch(side, travel, from_low):
72	    """travel = (extension, right, up); from_low = wrist started below the elbow.
73	
74	    An uppercut is an upward sweep from a low hand. None = too small or a retraction.
75	    """
76	    extension, right, up = travel
77	    if extension < -MIN_TRAVEL:
78	        return None  # arm folding back to guard
79	    inward = right if side == "L" else -right  # toward the body's centre line
80	    moves = {"STRAIGHT": extension, "HOOK": inward}
81	    if from_low:
82	        moves["UPPERCUT"] = up
83	    kind, amount = max(moves.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
84	    if amount < MIN_TRAVEL:
85	        return None  # too small, or a retraction (negative travel)
86	    return ("JAB" if side == LEAD else "CROSS") if kind == "STRAIGHT" else kind

88	
89	def body_state(img, world, sw_world, baseline):
90	    """Guard / dodge labels from the current pose."""
91	    states = []
92	    if baseline:
93	        drop = (img[NOSE][1] - baseline["nose"][1]) / baseline["sw"]
94	        shift = (img[NOSE][0] - baseline["nose"][0]) / baseline["sw"]
95	        if drop > DUCK_DROP:
96	            states.append("DUCK")
97	        if abs(shift) > SLIP_SHIFT:
98	            states.append("SLIP " + ("RIGHT" if shift > 0 else "LEFT"))

122	def level(world):
123	    """Rotate the skeleton so the torso is vertical, undoing camera pitch and roll."""
124	    torso = (world[L_SH] + world[R_SH]) / 2 - (world[L_HIP] + world[R_HIP]) / 2
125	    a, b = torso / (np.linalg.norm(torso) + 1e-6), np.array([0.0, -1.0, 0.0])
126	    v, c = np.cross(a, b), np.dot(a, b)
127	    k = np.array([[0, -v[2], v[1]], [v[2], 0, -v[0]], [-v[1], v[0], 0]])
128	    return world @ (np.eye(3) + k + k @ k / (1 + c)).T

132	    """Orthographic render of the world-space skeleton, rotated by yaw around the vertical axis."""
133	    canvas = np.zeros((size, size, 3), np.uint8)
134	    if min(vis[L_HIP], vis[R_HIP]) > 0.5:  # need the hips to find the torso
135	        world = level(world)
136	    c, s = np.cos(yaw), np.sin(yaw)
137	    x = -(world[:, 0] * c + world[:, 2] * s)  # negated to match the mirrored camera view
138	    px = (np.stack([x, world[:, 1]], axis=1) * scale + [size / 2, size * 0.55]).astype(int)
139	    for a, b in CONNECTIONS:
140	        if vis[a] > 0.4 and vis[b] > 0.4:

content.text:
This repo is a boxing motion tracker for a hackathon, with two separate inputs: an MPU6050 motion sensor on a glove, and a webcam. The three Python scripts don't import each other, so the glove and webcam data aren't combined yet. ## Python scripts | File | What it does | |---|---| | [punch_tracker.py](punch_tracker.py) | Reads sensor data from the Uno over USB serial. It has three commands:
• `capture`: records to CSV.
• `analyze`: finds punches, estimates their 3D paths and plots them.
• `live`: classifies each punch as it happens and presses a key on Windows, `w` for straight or `s` for one that travels up or down. `--dry-run` shows the result without pressing keys. | | [pose_tracker.py](pose_tracker.py) | Uses the webcam and MediaPipe to draw your skeleton and a rotatable 3D view. It detects jabs, crosses, hooks and uppercuts, plus duck, slip, block and guard-down. It downloads its pose model to `models/` on first run. | | [glove_receiver.py](glove_receiver.py) | Receives wireless glove data over UDP on port 5005 and syncs its timestamps to the laptop clock. It can tell gloves apart by IP address, but `GLOVE_BY_IP` is still empty. So far it only prints stats, and `--simulate` fakes a glove for testing without hardware. | ## Firmware | File | Board | What it does | |---|---|---| | [glove_imu.ino](firmware/glove_imu/glove_imu.ino) | ESP32-CAM | Wireless glove: samples the sensor at 500 Hz and sends it over WiFi to `glove_receiver.py`. | | [config.example.h](firmware/glove_imu/config.example.h) | ESP32-CAM | Template for your WiFi details. Copy it to `config.h`, which git ignores, or the sketch won't compile. | | [punch_stream.ino](firmware/punch_stream/punch_stream.ino) | Arduino Uno | Wired version: streams the same 500 Hz data over USB to `punch_tracker.py`. | | [sketch_nov6a.ino](firmware/sketch_nov6a/sketch_nov6a.ino) | Arduino Uno | Standalone test: shows roll, pitch and yaw on the Serial Plotter. Its text output and ±2 g range don't work with the Python scripts. | `glove_imu.ino` and `punch_stream.ino` send the same 19-byte data frame, and both Python receivers read that format. ## Config and project files | File | Purpose | |---|---| | [requirements.txt](requirements.txt) | Python dependencies, including the two I added (not committed yet). | | [README.md](README.md) | Only a title and one line, with no setup or usage instructions. | | [.gitignore](.gitignore) | Ignores `.venv/`, `models/`, `__pycache__/`, local Claude settings and the WiFi `config.h`. | | [.brainignore](.brainignore) | Keeps local Claude settings out of Entire's Brain index. | | [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) | Both point coding agents to the guide below. | | [.entire/agent-guide.md](.entire/agent-guide.md) | Workflow rules for agents using Entire's Graph and Brain tools. | | [.entire/settings.json](.entire/settings.json), [.entire/.gitignore](.entire/.gitignore) | Entire's settings and its ignore rules. | | [.claude/settings.json](.claude/settings.json) | Claude Code hooks for Entire (I only read the first 40 lines). | ## Gaps - **Wireless glove:** `punch_tracker.py` only reads from serial, so punch detection doesn't work on the WiFi stream yet. - **Live key presses:** `punch_tracker.py live` sends real keystrokes to whichever window has focus, so start with `--dry-run`. ## Corrections to my last message - **Run command:** `python punch_tracker.py` on its own just gives a usage error, because it needs a command, such as `python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7 --dry-run`. - **Arduino libraries:** the sketches don't need any third-party libraries. `glove_imu.ino` only needs the ESP32 board package and `config.h`, and the Uno sketches use the built-in `Wire` library.

That error means `pose_tracker.py` is running on your system Python, not `.venv`. System Python has no packages installed, while `cv2` is installed and working in `.venv`.

Run this from the project folder:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe pose_tracker.py
```

**To make plain `python` work in your terminal,** activate the environment first:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python pose_tracker.py
```
You should see `(.venv)` at the start of the prompt. You'll need to do this in each new terminal.

If PowerShell blocks the activate script, run this once, then activate again:
```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
```

**If you use the Run button in VS Code:**
1. Press `Ctrl+Shift+P`.
2. Run **Python: Select Interpreter**.
3. Choose the one under `.venv`, or browse to `.venv\Scripts\python.exe`.
4. Open a new terminal, because existing ones keep using the old Python.

If you'd rather not use a virtual environment, you can install the packages into system Python with `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`. I'd stick with `.venv`, since it keeps this project's packages separate from everything else.

# hack_trent_submission
Hack Trent Boxing Submission

A boxing motion tracker with two independent inputs: an MPU6050 motion sensor on a glove, and a webcam. The Python scripts don't import each other, so each one runs on its own and the glove and webcam data aren't combined yet.

## How the pieces connect

| Input | Runs on the board | Link | Runs on the laptop |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glove sensor, wired | `punch_stream.ino` on an Arduino Uno | USB serial at 500000 baud | `punch_tracker.py` |
| Glove sensor, wireless | `glove_imu.ino` on an ESP32-CAM | WiFi UDP on port 5005 | `glove_receiver.py` |
| Webcam | None | Camera 0 | `pose_tracker.py` |

The wired and wireless firmware send the same 19-byte frame, at 500 Hz:

```
A5 5A | timestamp in µs (uint32, little-endian) | ax ay az gx gy gz (int16, big-endian) | XOR of the timestamp and sensor bytes
```

Accelerometer range is ±16 g and gyro range is ±2000 deg/s. If you change these in the firmware, also change the matching constants in the Python script that reads it.

## Setup

Requires Python. These commands are for Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

If you see `ModuleNotFoundError`, the virtual environment isn't active. In VS Code, run **Python: Select Interpreter** and choose `.venv`.

## Python scripts

### `punch_tracker.py`

Reads the wired glove over USB serial, finds punches and estimates their paths. Replace `COM7` with your port.

```powershell
python punch_tracker.py capture --port COM7 --seconds 30 --out punches.csv
python punch_tracker.py analyze punches.csv
python punch_tracker.py analyze punches.csv --save punches.png
python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7 --dry-run
python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7
```

- **`capture`** records the raw sensor data to a CSV file.
- **`analyze`** finds punches in a recording, prints a table of each punch's speed and reach, and plots the 3D paths.
- **`live`** classifies each punch as it happens and presses a key: `w` for a straight punch, or `s` for one that travels up or down. This is Windows only.

Hold still for the first 2 seconds, and rest briefly between punches, because the script uses those rests to limit drift. Back-to-back combinations can't be reconstructed. Treat paths as rough estimates: compare shape and direction rather than exact distances.

> **Warning:** without `--dry-run`, `live` sends real keystrokes to whichever window has focus.

### `pose_tracker.py`

Tracks your body through the webcam with MediaPipe and shows a skeleton overlay plus a rotatable 3D view. It detects jabs, crosses, hooks and uppercuts, plus duck, slip, block and guard-down. On first run, it downloads its pose model to `models/`, so it needs internet access once.

```powershell
python pose_tracker.py
```

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `c` | Calibrate while standing in guard, which is needed for duck and slip detection |
| `a` / `d` | Rotate the 3D view |
| `q` | Quit |

The lead hand defaults to left (orthodox). To change it, set `LEAD` at the top of the file.

### `glove_receiver.py`

Receives the wireless glove's data over UDP, and puts each sample on the laptop's clock. Run directly, it prints the sample rate, peak acceleration and gyro readings. Other code can use its `GloveReceiver` class to read samples, but no script in this repo does that yet.

```powershell
python glove_receiver.py             # listen for a real glove
python glove_receiver.py --simulate  # fake a glove, with no hardware needed
```

To tell two gloves apart, add their IP addresses to `GLOVE_BY_IP`. Any glove not listed is treated as `L`. If the sensor is mounted at an angle, set `AXIS_MAP` and `AXIS_SIGN`.

## Firmware

The Uno sketches use only the built-in `Wire` library. `glove_imu.ino` needs the ESP32 board package (core 3.x). Each sketch lists its wiring at the top of the file.

| File | Board | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `firmware/punch_stream/punch_stream.ino` | Arduino Uno | Streams sensor data over USB to `punch_tracker.py`. Close the Serial Monitor first, because only one program can use the port. |
| `firmware/glove_imu/glove_imu.ino` | AI Thinker ESP32-CAM | Sends sensor data over WiFi to `glove_receiver.py`. The camera isn't used. |
| `firmware/glove_imu/config.example.h` | ESP32-CAM | Template for your WiFi details. Copy it to `config.h` in the same folder and fill it in, or `glove_imu.ino` won't compile. Git ignores `config.h`, so your password stays on your computer. |
| `firmware/sketch_nov6a/sketch_nov6a.ino` | Arduino Uno | Sensor test that shows roll, pitch and yaw on the Serial Plotter at 115200 baud. Its output doesn't work with the Python scripts. Yaw drifts over time. |

## Project files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `requirements.txt` | Python packages for all three scripts. |
| `.gitignore` | Keeps `.venv/`, `models/`, `__pycache__/`, `config.h` and local Claude settings out of git. |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` | Point coding agents to the Entire guide below. |
| `.entire/agent-guide.md` | Tells coding agents how to use Entire's Graph and Brain tools in this repo. |
| `.entire/settings.json` | Turns on Entire and sets where it stores session checkpoints. |
| `.entire/.gitignore` | Keeps Entire's local logs, metadata and temporary files out of git. |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Claude Code hooks that connect sessions and edits to Entire. |
| `.brainignore` | Keeps local Claude settings out of Entire's Brain index. |

# hack_trent_submission
Hack Trent Boxing Submission

A boxing motion tracker with two independent inputs: an MPU6050 motion sensor on a glove, and a webcam. The Python scripts don't import each other, so each one runs on its own and the glove and webcam data aren't combined yet.

## How the pieces connect

| Input | Runs on the board | Link | Runs on the laptop |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glove sensor, wired | `punch_stream.ino` on an Arduino Uno | USB serial at 500000 baud | `punch_tracker.py` |
| Glove sensor, wireless | `glove_imu.ino` on an ESP32-CAM | WiFi UDP on port 5005 | `glove_receiver.py` |
| Webcam | None | Camera 0 | `pose_tracker.py` |

The wired and wireless firmware send the same 19-byte frame, at 500 Hz:

```
A5 5A | timestamp in µs (uint32, little-endian) | ax ay az gx gy gz (int16, big-endian) | XOR of the timestamp and sensor bytes
```

Accelerometer range is ±16 g and gyro range is ±2000 deg/s. If you change these in the firmware, also change the matching constants in the Python script that reads it.

## Setup

Requires Python. These commands are for Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

If you see `ModuleNotFoundError`, the virtual environment isn't active. In VS Code, run **Python: Select Interpreter** and choose `.venv`.

## Python scripts

### `punch_tracker.py`

Reads the wired glove over USB serial, finds punches and estimates their paths. Replace `COM7` with your port.

```powershell
python punch_tracker.py capture --port COM7 --seconds 30 --out punches.csv
python punch_tracker.py analyze punches.csv
python punch_tracker.py analyze punches.csv --save punches.png
python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7 --dry-run
python punch_tracker.py live --port COM7
```

- **`capture`** records the raw sensor data to a CSV file.
- **`analyze`** finds punches in a recording, prints a table of each punch's speed and reach, and plots the 3D paths.
- **`live`** classifies each punch as it happens and presses a key: `w` for a straight punch, or `s` for one that travels up or down. This is Windows only.

Hold still for the first 2 seconds, and rest briefly between punches, because the script uses those rests to limit drift. Back-to-back combinations can't be reconstructed. Treat paths as rough estimates: compare shape and direction rather than exact distances.

> **Warning:** without `--dry-run`, `live` sends real keystrokes to whichever window has focus.

### `pose_tracker.py`

Tracks your body through the webcam with MediaPipe and shows a skeleton overlay plus a rotatable 3D view. It detects jabs, crosses, hooks and uppercuts, plus duck, slip, block and guard-down. On first run, it downloads its pose model to `models/`, so it needs internet access once.

```powershell
python pose_tracker.py
```

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `c` | Calibrate while standing in guard, which is needed for duck and slip detection |
| `a` / `d` | Rotate the 3D view |
| `q` | Quit |

The lead hand defaults to left (orthodox). To change it, set `LEAD` at the top of the file.

### `glove_receiver.py`

Receives the wireless glove's data over UDP, and puts each sample on the laptop's clock. Run directly, it prints the sample rate, peak acceleration and gyro readings. Other code can use its `GloveReceiver` class to read samples, but no script in this repo does that yet.

```powershell
python glove_receiver.py             # listen for a real glove
python glove_receiver.py --simulate  # fake a glove, with no hardware needed
```

To tell two gloves apart, add their IP addresses to `GLOVE_BY_IP`. Any glove not listed is treated as `L`. If the sensor is mounted at an angle, set `AXIS_MAP` and `AXIS_SIGN`.

## Firmware

The Uno sketches use only the built-in `Wire` library. `glove_imu.ino` needs the ESP32 board package (core 3.x). Each sketch lists its wiring at the top of the file.

| File | Board | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `firmware/punch_stream/punch_stream.ino` | Arduino Uno | Streams sensor data over USB to `punch_tracker.py`. Close the Serial Monitor first, because only one program can use the port. |
| `firmware/glove_imu/glove_imu.ino` | AI Thinker ESP32-CAM | Sends sensor data over WiFi to `glove_receiver.py`. The camera isn't used. |
| `firmware/glove_imu/config.example.h` | ESP32-CAM | Template for your WiFi details. Copy it to `config.h` in the same folder and fill it in, or `glove_imu.ino` won't compile. Git ignores `config.h`, so your password stays on your computer. |
| `firmware/sketch_nov6a/sketch_nov6a.ino` | Arduino Uno | Sensor test that shows roll, pitch and yaw on the Serial Plotter at 115200 baud. Its output doesn't work with the Python scripts. Yaw drifts over time. |

## Project files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `requirements.txt` | Python packages for all three scripts. |
| `.gitignore` | Keeps `.venv/`, `models/`, `__pycache__/`, `config.h` and local Claude settings out of git. |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` | Point coding agents to the Entire guide below. |
| `.entire/agent-guide.md` | Tells coding agents how to use Entire's Graph and Brain tools in this repo. |
| `.entire/settings.json` | Turns on Entire and sets where it stores session checkpoints. |
| `.entire/.gitignore` | Keeps Entire's local logs, metadata and temporary files out of git. |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Claude Code hooks that connect sessions and edits to Entire. |
| `.brainignore` | Keeps local Claude settings out of Entire's Brain index. |

=== glove_punch.py
"""Detect punches from glove motion-sensor data, and use them to confirm the camera's punches.

A punch is a short, hard burst of acceleration. We measure how far the total acceleration is from
1 g (gravity), so it does not matter how the glove is tilted. The burst starts when that crosses
START_G and ends when it falls back under END_G. The sensor reports about 200 times a second, far more
often than the camera sees frames, so the glove gives a precise time and a real impact strength.

The glove cannot tell a jab from a hook, so it never chooses the key. The camera does that. The glove
only answers "did this hand really punch just now?", which filters out the camera mistaking a wave
or a reach for a punch.

These numbers are starting points taken from the simulator. Tune them against the real glove.
"""
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

START_G = 3.0         # acceleration beyond gravity that starts a punch
END_G = 1.5           # the punch is over when it falls back below this
COOLDOWN = 0.25       # seconds before the same glove can start another punch
MAX_DURATION = 0.4    # a burst longer than this is reported anyway (shaking, not one punch)


@dataclass
=== punch_detector.py
"""Decide when a punch happened and what kind it was, from the wrist-motion numbers pose_tracker measures.

pose_tracker gives, every frame and for each hand: the wrist speed, and how far the wrist moved
(extension, sideways, up) over the last few frames. This module turns that stream into punch events.

How it differs from the check built into pose_tracker.py, which looks at one frame at a time:
  - A punch is a burst. We wait until the hand has been fast for a few frames and its speed has just
    started to fall (the peak has passed), then judge the whole burst. Judging the first fast frame,
    when the hand has barely moved, mislabels punches.
  - People wind up before a punch (the hand drops or pulls back) and swing back to guard after it.
    Those bursts match no punch, so they are ignored and do not stop the real punch that follows.
  - One punch locks that hand out briefly, so the swing back to guard is not counted as another punch.
  - Raising both hands to guard at once looks like two uppercuts. It is ignored.
  - Straight punches (jab, cross) are not detected. A webcam facing you cannot see an arm extending
    straight toward it: in recorded sessions the arm moved only 0.1 shoulder-widths and its speed was
    no higher than the camera's own jitter. Set straight_ext to try anyway.

The numbers are shoulder-widths and seconds, taken from a recorded session. Tune with tune_punches.py
and replay_punches.py.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Settings:
=== game_input.py
"""Turn boxing events into keyboard input, so existing games can be played with your body.

Two kinds of key output:
  tap  - a punch. The key is pressed, then released a few milliseconds later. Games read the key
         state once per frame, so a press that is released instantly can be missed.
  hold - a body state (block, duck, slip). The key stays down while the state lasts.

Keys are sent as hardware scan codes with the Windows SendInput call. Browsers and DirectInput games
accept these; many games ignore the plain virtual-key events that most keyboard libraries send.

The event names are the labels pose_tracker.py already produces: JAB, CROSS, HOOK, UPPERCUT for
punches and BLOCK, DUCK, SLIP LEFT, SLIP RIGHT, GUARD DOWN for body states. A mapping file (see
mappings/) says which key each one presses.

Run `python game_input.py` for a dry run that only prints. `--live` really presses keys.
"""
import argparse
import atexit
import ctypes
import json
import os
import sys
import threading
import time

    parser.add_argument("--simulate-glove", action="store_true",
                        help="like --glove, but with a fake glove that punches every 1.5 s (for testing)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    mapping = game_input.Mapping.load(args.mapping)
    keyboard = game_input.SendInputKeyboard() if args.live else game_input.DryRunKeyboard()
    game = game_input.GameInput(mapping, keyboard)
    game.set_enabled(not args.live)  # a dry run is harmless, so it starts on; live starts off

    print("LIVE: keys go to the focused window." if args.live else "Dry run: nothing is pressed.")
    print(f"Key output is {'ON' if game.enabled else 'OFF'}. F7 calibrates, F8 toggles output, F9 quits.")

    if not args.builtin_punches:
        print("Camera punches: HOOK and UPPERCUT are detected. Straight punches (jab, cross) are not: a webcam")
        print("facing you cannot see them. Use a glove for those, or press the jab/cross keys by hand.")

    glove = None
    if args.glove or args.simulate_glove:
        import threading
        import glove_punch
        import glove_receiver
        receiver = glove_receiver.GloveReceiver()
        if args.simulate_glove:
            threading.Thread(target=glove_receiver.simulate, daemon=True).start()
        glove = glove_punch.GlovePunches(receiver)
        print("Glove: listening on UDP port 5005. Camera punches need a matching glove punch.")

    import pose_tracker  # imported here so the rest of this file works without OpenCV or MediaPipe
    callbacks = make_callbacks(game, Hotkeys(), glove=glove, detector=False if args.builtin_punches else None)
    try:
        pose_tracker.main(**callbacks)

--- glove_punch GlovePunches


class GlovePunches:
    """Watches every glove a GloveReceiver hears and remembers each one's latest punch."""

    def __init__(self, receiver, **detector_settings):
        self.receiver, self.settings = receiver, detector_settings
        self.detectors, self.seen_t, self.last = {}, {}, {}

    def poll(self):
        """Run any new samples through the detectors. Returns a list of (glove, Punch)."""
        found = []
        for glove, buffer in list(self.receiver.samples.items()):
            detector = self.detectors.setdefault(glove, PunchDetector(**self.settings))
            seen = self.seen_t.get(glove, -1.0)
            samples = list(buffer)
            if samples and samples[-1].t < seen - 5:  # the glove rebooted and its clock restarted
                seen = -1.0
            for sample in samples:
                if sample.t > seen:
                    seen = sample.t
                    punch = detector.update(sample)
                    if punch:
                        self.last[glove] = punch
                        found.append((glove, punch))
            self.seen_t[glove] = seen
        return found

    def confirms(self, glove, within=0.6, now=None):
        """True if this hand punched in the last `within` seconds.

        A hand with no glove (nothing heard from it) is never blocked, so a single glove still works.
        """
        if glove not in self.receiver.samples:
            return True
        detector = self.detectors.get(glove)
        if detector is not None and detector.active:
            return True  # a punch is happening right now and has not finished yet
        punch = self.last.get(glove)
        now = time.time() if now is None else now
        return punch is not None and -0.1 <= now - punch.t <= within

content.text:
**There is now: `controller.py` on `main` uses both the glove and the webcam.** It arrived with Kadir's branch, merged as PR #4. It only combines them if you turn the glove on, and I've read this code but haven't run it:

```powershell
python controller.py --glove            # real glove, dry run
python controller.py --simulate-glove   # fake glove, no hardware needed
python controller.py --glove --live     # really presses keys
```

**How it combines them:** the webcam decides what kind of punch happened, and the glove only confirms it. If the webcam sees a punch but that hand's glove felt nothing in the last 0.6 seconds or so, the punch is ignored. The two readings aren't merged into a single estimate of the motion.

**Limitations:**
- **No jabs or crosses by default:** the camera detector has straight punches turned off, because a webcam facing you can't see them well. The glove only confirms punches the camera has already reported, so it can't trigger these on its own. The startup message says "Use a glove for those", but from what I read, that doesn't work yet.
- **Wireless glove only:** it uses `glove_receiver.py`, so the Uno setup and `punch_tracker.py` aren't involved. The 3D path and angle estimates in `punch_tracker.py` aren't used either.
- **Glove side:** `GLOVE_BY_IP` is empty, so any glove counts as the left hand. A glove on your right hand would filter your left-hand punches, while right-hand punches would go through unchecked. A hand with no glove detected is never filtered, so add the glove's IP address to that setting.

**The README I wrote is now wrong:**
- **Line 4:** says the scripts don't import each other and the data isn't combined.
- **Line 74:** says no script uses `GloveReceiver`.
- **Missing files:** it doesn't cover `controller.py`, `game_input.py`, `glove_punch.py`, `glove_check.py`, `punch_detector.py`, `replay_punches.py`, `tune_punches.py` or `mappings/browser_boxing.json`.

It was accurate for the files I checked, but PR #4 merged before it did. Do you want me to read Kadir's files and update the README on a new branch? I can also make the glove trigger jabs and crosses, but check with Kadir first, since those are Kadir's files.

entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, repository
context, docs, history, code-index records, and durable memories, then exposes
retrieval, verification, and evaluation surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Set up the brain & agents:
  setup              Build the brain and start background updates
  add                Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  agent-guide        Preview repository-specific agent instructions
  webhook            Notify another service when this brain changes
  config             Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

Search & explore the brain:
  overview           Summarize the project, its structure, and decisions
  brief              Gather relevant context for a task
  query              Search the brain (BM25 lexical ranking)
  get                Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get          Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash               Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

Durable memories & patterns:
  recall             Retrieve durable memories matching a query for the current branch
  remember           Record a durable memory about this repository
  distill            Extract durable memories from sessions (requires an agent)
  memories           Inspect, retract, and garbage-collect durable memories
  connect            Bind this repository to its hosted brain explicitly
  disconnect         Stop syncing this repository with its hosted brain
  verify             Verify durable memory anchors against local retained sources
  patterns           Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Code index & context:
  inspect            Explore code, dependencies, and change history
  show               Show one code-index record
  viz                Explore the brain as a graph in your browser

Brain state & maintenance:
  status             Show brain coverage, freshness, and workspace state
  stats              Show brain record counts and breakdowns

Workspaces & sharing:
  workspace          Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces
  bundle             Import or export local brain bundles

Troubleshooting & operations:
  memories import    Import durable memories from another memory tool's export
  memories sync      Sync this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
  memories gc        Prune retracted and old superseded memories; report orphans
  memories vitality  Show serve receipts per memory (which memories the read surfaces actually emitted)
  memory             Manage conversation indexing and background jobs
  entities           Find checkpoints and sessions that changed a symbol
  repair             Rebuild Graph's committed-tree code index
  docs               Inspect how non-code documents are read into the brain
  refresh            Create or refresh the repository brain
  watch              Keep the brain up to date automatically
  stop               Pause background brain work on this machine
  start              Resume background brain work paused by `stop`
  reset              Remove local generated brain data
  repo-identity      Find and resolve conflicting brain stores

Miscellaneous:
  path               Print the persistent brain path for a repo path or URL
  capabilities       List supported features and retrieval sources
  doctor             Diagnose environment and brain pipeline problems
  version            Print plugin version
  help               Help about any command

Flags:
  -h, --help       help for entire-brain
      --help-all   List all commands, including hidden commands
  -v, --version    version for entire-brain

Use "entire-brain [command] --help" for more information about a command.
--- remember
Record a durable memory about this repository

Usage:
  entire-brain remember <memory> [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                Agent used to classify when --path is omitted: auto, codex, claude-code, ollama, command, or none (default "auto")
      --agent-command stringArray   Agent command argv for --agent command
      --branch string               Branch to store the memory on (default: current branch)
      --global                      Record the memory globally, so every repository recalls it
  -h, --help                        help for remember
      --json                        Emit the created memory as JSON
      --kind string                 Memory kind: decision|invariant|gotcha|preference|convention. If omitted, it is inferred
      --model string                Model for codex/claude-code/ollama classification
      --path string                 Taxonomy path(s), comma-separated (e.g. preferences.coding.style). If omitted, the agent classifies the memory
      --session string              Session id the memory was authored in (default: $ENTIRE_BRAIN_SESSION_ID); agent and hook callers pass it so the memory carries session provenance

Exit code 1
sync exchanges this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
over the per-fact wire: push this branch's memories, pull the team's delta feed.
It is the same exchange the background sync runs, except failures fail the
command instead of degrading silently.

Memory sync is hosted-only. The default target is the connected binding
('entire brain connect'); on an unconnected repo a plain sync fails and
memories stay local. The local-gitmeta backend was removed (COR-2236):
--memories-backend accepts only "http", and the explicit target resolves
flag > env > connected binding (--api-url/ENTIRE_API_URL,
--repo-id/ENTIRE_REPO_ID, --token/ENTIRE_API_TOKEN; on a connected repo the
binding supplies the target and the token is minted automatically).

ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS (or its deprecated alias ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY)
suppresses all hosted sync regardless of defaults and flags.

Usage:
  entire-brain memories sync [flags]

Flags:
      --api-url string            Entire API base URL, https:// (overrides ENTIRE_API_URL)
      --branch string             Branch to sync (default: current branch)
  -h, --help                      help for sync
      --json                      Emit the sync result as JSON
      --memories-backend string   Memory-set backend; only "http" (the hosted per-fact wire) is supported
      --repo-id string            Target repo id (overrides ENTIRE_REPO_ID)
      --token string              Entire API bearer token (overrides ENTIRE_API_TOKEN)
=== connect
connect binds this repository to its hosted brain: it records the repo id and
API base URL (non-secrets only — the host CLI's own login mints a fresh token
per sync), then runs one immediate sync so the first pull happens right away.

Running connect (or the onboarding flow) is the ONLY way a repository starts
syncing: by default memories stay local and background triggers never connect
a repo on their own. Placement resolves through the host CLI (entire repo
view); pass --repo-id and --api-url to bypass resolution — a non-default cell
or a staging target. Re-running connect re-joins after 'entire brain
disconnect'.

Usage:
  entire-brain connect [flags]

Flags:
