1	"""Webcam pose tracking: skeleton overlay, guard/dodge state and punch types.
2	
3	Punches are measured in a body frame (forward / sideways / up) built from MediaPipe's
4	3D world landmarks, so they work at any angle to the camera.
5	Keys: c = calibrate or recalibrate (stand in guard), a/d = rotate the 3D view, q = quit.
6	"""
7	import os
8	import time
9	import urllib.request
10	from collections import deque
11	
12	import cv2
13	import mediapipe as mp
14	import numpy as np
15	from mediapipe.tasks import python as mp_python
16	from mediapipe.tasks.python import vision
17	
18	MODEL_URL = (
19	    "https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/pose_landmarker/"
20	    "pose_landmarker_full/float16/latest/pose_landmarker_full.task"
21	)
22	MODEL_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "models", "pose_landmarker_full.task")
23	
24	NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, R_EL, L_WR, R_WR, L_HIP, R_HIP = 0, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 23, 24
25	CONNECTIONS = [
26	    (11, 12), (11, 13), (13, 15), (12, 14), (14, 16), (11, 23), (12, 24), (23, 24),
27	    (23, 25), (24, 26), (25, 27), (26, 28), (0, 11), (0, 12),
28	]
29	
30	# Tunables. Distances are in shoulder-widths so they work at any range.
31	GUARD_DIST = 1.0        # wrist this close to the nose => hand is up
32	DUCK_DROP = 0.45        # nose below baseline by this much => duck
33	SLIP_SHIFT = 0.5        # nose sideways from baseline by this much => slip
34	PUNCH_SPEED = 4.0       # wrist speed (shoulder-widths/s) that starts a punch
35	MIN_TRAVEL = 0.4        # wrist travel (shoulder-widths) needed to call a punch type
36	PUNCH_COOLDOWN = 0.25   # seconds
37	LEAD = "L"              # lead hand throws the jab (orthodox = "L")
38	
39	
40	def ensure_model():
41	    if not os.path.exists(MODEL_PATH):
42	        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(MODEL_PATH), exist_ok=True)
43	        print("Downloading pose model...")
44	        urllib.request.urlretrieve(MODEL_URL, MODEL_PATH)
45	
46	
47	class Smoother:
48	    """Exponential moving average over a landmark array."""
49	
50	    def __init__(self, alpha):
51	        self.alpha, self.prev = alpha, None
52	
53	    def __call__(self, x):
54	        self.prev = x if self.prev is None else self.alpha * x + (1 - self.alpha) * self.prev
55	        return self.prev
56	
57	
58	def punch_travel(delta, start, end, world, sw):
59	    """Per hand (extension, right, up) in shoulder-widths.
60	
61	    delta = wrist movement relative to the shoulder; start/end = wrist-to-shoulder vectors.
62	    Extension is how much the arm straightened, so it needs no facing direction.
63	    """
64	    right = world[R_SH] - world[L_SH]
65	    right[1] = 0
66	    right /= np.linalg.norm(right) + 1e-6
67	    extension = (np.linalg.norm(end, axis=1) - np.linalg.norm(start, axis=1)) / sw
68	    return np.stack([extension, delta @ right, -delta[:, 1]], axis=1)
69	
70	
71	def classify_punch(side, travel, from_low):
72	    """travel = (extension, right, up); from_low = wrist started below the elbow.
73	
74	    An uppercut is an upward sweep from a low hand. None = too small or a retraction.
75	    """
76	    extension, right, up = travel
77	    if extension < -MIN_TRAVEL:
78	        return None  # arm folding back to guard
79	    inward = right if side == "L" else -right  # toward the body's centre line
80	    moves = {"STRAIGHT": extension, "HOOK": inward}
81	    if from_low:
82	        moves["UPPERCUT"] = up
83	    kind, amount = max(moves.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
84	    if amount < MIN_TRAVEL:
85	        return None  # too small, or a retraction (negative travel)
86	    return ("JAB" if side == LEAD else "CROSS") if kind == "STRAIGHT" else kind
87	
88	
89	def body_state(img, world, sw_world, baseline):
90	    """Guard / dodge labels from the current pose."""
91	    states = []
92	    if baseline:
93	        drop = (img[NOSE][1] - baseline["nose"][1]) / baseline["sw"]
94	        shift = (img[NOSE][0] - baseline["nose"][0]) / baseline["sw"]
95	        if drop > DUCK_DROP:
96	            states.append("DUCK")
97	        if abs(shift) > SLIP_SHIFT:
98	            states.append("SLIP " + ("RIGHT" if shift > 0 else "LEFT"))
99	    up = [np.linalg.norm(world[i] - world[NOSE]) / sw_world < GUARD_DIST for i in (L_WR, R_WR)]
100	    if all(up):
101	        states.append("BLOCK")
102	    elif not any(up):
103	        states.append("GUARD DOWN")
104	    return states
105	
106	
107	def draw(frame, img, vis, flash, now):
108	    h, w = frame.shape[:2]
109	    px = (img * [w, h]).astype(int)
110	    for a, b in CONNECTIONS:
111	        if vis[a] > 0.4 and vis[b] > 0.4:
112	            cv2.line(frame, tuple(px[a]), tuple(px[b]), (0, 255, 0), 3)
113	    for i in (NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, R_EL, L_WR, R_WR):
114	        cv2.circle(frame, tuple(px[i]), 6, (0, 200, 255), -1)
115	    for side, idx in (("L", L_WR), ("R", R_WR)):
116	        text, t = flash[side]
117	        if now - t < 0.6:
118	            cv2.putText(frame, text, (px[idx][0] + 10, px[idx][1] - 10),
119	                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.9, (0, 0, 255), 2)
120	
121	
122	def level(world):
123	    """Rotate the skeleton so the torso is vertical, undoing camera pitch and roll."""
124	    torso = (world[L_SH] + world[R_SH]) / 2 - (world[L_HIP] + world[R_HIP]) / 2
125	    a, b = torso / (np.linalg.norm(torso) + 1e-6), np.array([0.0, -1.0, 0.0])
126	    v, c = np.cross(a, b), np.dot(a, b)
127	    k = np.array([[0, -v[2], v[1]], [v[2], 0, -v[0]], [-v[1], v[0], 0]])
128	    return world @ (np.eye(3) + k + k @ k / (1 + c)).T
129	
130	
131	def draw_3d(world, vis, yaw, size=480, scale=250):
132	    """Orthographic render of the world-space skeleton, rotated by yaw around the vertical axis."""
133	    canvas = np.zeros((size, size, 3), np.uint8)
134	    if min(vis[L_HIP], vis[R_HIP]) > 0.5:  # need the hips to find the torso
135	        world = level(world)
136	    c, s = np.cos(yaw), np.sin(yaw)
137	    x = -(world[:, 0] * c + world[:, 2] * s)  # negated to match the mirrored camera view
138	    px = (np.stack([x, world[:, 1]], axis=1) * scale + [size / 2, size * 0.55]).astype(int)
139	    for a, b in CONNECTIONS:
140	        if vis[a] > 0.4 and vis[b] > 0.4:
141	            cv2.line(canvas, tuple(px[a]), tuple(px[b]), (0, 255, 0), 3)
142	    for i in (NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, R_EL):
143	        cv2.circle(canvas, tuple(px[i]), 6, (0, 200, 255), -1)
144	    for i in (L_WR, R_WR):
145	        cv2.circle(canvas, tuple(px[i]), 10, (0, 0, 255), -1)
146	    return canvas
147	
148	
149	def main(on_punch=None, on_states=None, on_frame=None, want_calibrate=None, on_calibrated=None,
150	         on_features=None, on_draw=None, builtin_punches=True):
151	    """Run the tracker. Run on its own it only draws; the callbacks let other code react.
152	
153	    on_punch(kind, side, speed): a punch was recognised. kind is JAB, CROSS, HOOK or UPPERCUT.
154	    on_states(states): called every frame with the body-state labels active right now (BLOCK, DUCK,
155	        SLIP LEFT, SLIP RIGHT, GUARD DOWN). It gets an empty list when nobody is in view.
156	    on_frame(): called every frame; return True to stop the tracker.
157	    want_calibrate(): called every frame; return True to calibrate now. This lets a hotkey recalibrate
158	        while another window (the game) has focus. The c key in the camera window always works too.
159	    on_calibrated(): called after a successful calibration.
160	    on_features(now, speeds, travel, from_low): the raw numbers the punch decision uses, every frame.
161	        speeds = [left, right] wrist speed; travel = 2x3 array of (extension, right, up) per hand;
162	        from_low = [left, right] wrist started below the elbow. It may return a list of (side, kind)
163	        punches it decided; those are shown on screen and passed to on_punch.
164	    on_draw(frame): draw extra text on the camera image before it is shown.
165	    builtin_punches: set False to switch off this file's own punch check, so only the punches
166	        returned by on_features count (see punch_detector.py).
167	    """
168	    ensure_model()
169	    landmarker = vision.PoseLandmarker.create_from_options(vision.PoseLandmarkerOptions(
170	        base_options=mp_python.BaseOptions(model_asset_path=MODEL_PATH),
171	        running_mode=vision.RunningMode.VIDEO,
172	        min_pose_detection_confidence=0.4,
173	        min_pose_presence_confidence=0.4,
174	        min_tracking_confidence=0.4,
175	    ))
176	    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)
177	    if not cap.isOpened():
178	        raise SystemExit("Could not open webcam")
179	
180	    smooth_img, smooth_world = Smoother(0.6), Smoother(0.7)
181	    yaw = 0.0  # 3D view rotation
182	    cv2.namedWindow("3D skeleton")
183	    cv2.moveWindow("3D skeleton", 700, 50)  # beside the camera window, not on top of it
184	    history = deque(maxlen=5)  # (time, wrist-relative-to-shoulder, wrist-below-elbow), ~0.2 s
185	    baseline = None
186	    calibrated_at = -10.0  # when the last calibration happened, for the on-screen flash
187	    last_punch = {"L": 0.0, "R": 0.0}
188	    flash = {"L": ("", 0.0), "R": ("", 0.0)}
189	    t0 = time.time()
190	
191	    failed_reads = 0
192	    while True:
193	        ok, frame = cap.read()
194	        if not ok or frame is None:
195	            # Some webcams return empty frames for the first moment after opening. Wait before giving up.
196	            failed_reads += 1
197	            if failed_reads > 150:  # about 3 seconds of nothing
198	                break
199	            time.sleep(0.02)
200	            continue
201	        failed_reads = 0
202	        now = time.time()
203	        rgb = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
204	        result = landmarker.detect_for_video(
205	            mp.Image(image_format=mp.ImageFormat.SRGB, data=rgb), int((now - t0) * 1000))
206	        frame = cv2.flip(frame, 1)  # mirror for display only; image x is flipped to match
207	        lines = ["no body detected"]
208	
209	        if result.pose_landmarks:
210	            lm = result.pose_landmarks[0]
211	            img = smooth_img(np.array([[1 - p.x, p.y] for p in lm]))
212	            vis = np.array([p.visibility for p in lm])
213	            world = smooth_world(np.array([[p.x, p.y, p.z] for p in result.pose_world_landmarks[0]]))
214	            sw = np.linalg.norm(world[L_SH] - world[R_SH]) + 1e-6
215	
216	            wrist_below_elbow = world[[L_WR, R_WR], 1] > world[[L_EL, R_EL], 1]  # world y points down
217	            history.append((now, world[[L_WR, R_WR]] - world[[L_SH, R_SH]], wrist_below_elbow))
218	            dt = now - history[0][0]
219	            speeds = [0.0, 0.0]
220	            if dt > 0:
221	                delta = (history[-1][1] - history[0][1]) / sw
222	                travel = punch_travel(delta, history[0][1], history[-1][1], world, sw)
223	                for i, side in enumerate("LR"):
224	                    speeds[i] = np.linalg.norm(delta[i]) / dt
225	                    if builtin_punches and speeds[i] > PUNCH_SPEED and now - last_punch[side] > PUNCH_COOLDOWN:
226	                        kind = classify_punch(side, travel[i], history[0][2][i])

"""Webcam pose tracking: skeleton overlay, guard/dodge state and punch types.

Punches are measured in a body frame (forward / sideways / up) built from MediaPipe's
3D world landmarks, so they work at any angle to the camera.
Keys: c = calibrate or recalibrate (stand in guard), a/d = rotate the 3D view, q = quit.
"""
import os
import time
import urllib.request
from collections import deque

import cv2
import mediapipe as mp
import numpy as np
from mediapipe.tasks import python as mp_python
from mediapipe.tasks.python import vision

MODEL_URL = (
    "https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/pose_landmarker/"
    "pose_landmarker_full/float16/latest/pose_landmarker_full.task"
)
MODEL_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "models", "pose_landmarker_full.task")

NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, R_EL, L_WR, R_WR, L_HIP, R_HIP = 0, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 23, 24
CONNECTIONS = [
    (11, 12), (11, 13), (13, 15), (12, 14), (14, 16), (11, 23), (12, 24), (23, 24),
    (23, 25), (24, 26), (25, 27), (26, 28), (0, 11), (0, 12),
]

# Tunables. Distances are in shoulder-widths so they work at any range.
GUARD_DIST = 1.0        # wrist this close to the nose => hand is up
DUCK_DROP = 0.45        # nose below baseline by this much => duck
SLIP_SHIFT = 0.5        # nose sideways from baseline by this much => slip
PUNCH_SPEED = 4.0       # wrist speed (shoulder-widths/s) that starts a punch
MIN_TRAVEL = 0.4        # wrist travel (shoulder-widths) needed to call a punch type
PUNCH_COOLDOWN = 0.25   # seconds
LEAD = "L"              # lead hand throws the jab (orthodox = "L")


def ensure_model():
    if not os.path.exists(MODEL_PATH):
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(MODEL_PATH), exist_ok=True)
        print("Downloading pose model...")
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(MODEL_URL, MODEL_PATH)


class Smoother:
    """Exponential moving average over a landmark array."""

    def __init__(self, alpha):
        self.alpha, self.prev = alpha, None

    def __call__(self, x):
        self.prev = x if self.prev is None else self.alpha * x + (1 - self.alpha) * self.prev
        return self.prev


def punch_travel(delta, start, end, world, sw):
    """Per hand (extension, right, up) in shoulder-widths.

    delta = wrist movement relative to the shoulder; start/end = wrist-to-shoulder vectors.
    Extension is how much the arm straightened, so it needs no facing direction.
    """
    right = world[R_SH] - world[L_SH]
    right[1] = 0
    right /= np.linalg.norm(right) + 1e-6
    extension = (np.linalg.norm(end, axis=1) - np.linalg.norm(start, axis=1)) / sw
    return np.stack([extension, delta @ right, -delta[:, 1]], axis=1)


def classify_punch(side, travel, from_low):
    """travel = (extension, right, up); from_low = wrist started below the elbow.

    An uppercut is an upward sweep from a low hand. None = too small or a retraction.
    """
    extension, right, up = travel
    if extension < -MIN_TRAVEL:
        return None  # arm folding back to guard
    inward = right if side == "L" else -right  # toward the body's centre line
    moves = {"STRAIGHT": extension, "HOOK": inward}
    if from_low:
        moves["UPPERCUT"] = up
    kind, amount = max(moves.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
    if amount < MIN_TRAVEL:
        return None  # too small, or a retraction (negative travel)
    return ("JAB" if side == LEAD else "CROSS") if kind == "STRAIGHT" else kind


def body_state(img, world, sw_world, baseline):
    """Guard / dodge labels from the current pose."""
    states = []
    if baseline:
        drop = (img[NOSE][1] - baseline["nose"][1]) / baseline["sw"]
        shift = (img[NOSE][0] - baseline["nose"][0]) / baseline["sw"]
        if drop > DUCK_DROP:
            states.append("DUCK")
        if abs(shift) > SLIP_SHIFT:
            states.append("SLIP " + ("RIGHT" if shift > 0 else "LEFT"))
    up = [np.linalg.norm(world[i] - world[NOSE]) / sw_world < GUARD_DIST for i in (L_WR, R_WR)]
    if all(up):
        states.append("BLOCK")
    elif not any(up):
        states.append("GUARD DOWN")
    return states


def draw(frame, img, vis, flash, now):
    h, w = frame.shape[:2]
    px = (img * [w, h]).astype(int)
    for a, b in CONNECTIONS:
        if vis[a] > 0.4 and vis[b] > 0.4:
            cv2.line(frame, tuple(px[a]), tuple(px[b]), (0, 255, 0), 3)
    for i in (NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, R_EL, L_WR, R_WR):
        cv2.circle(frame, tuple(px[i]), 6, (0, 200, 255), -1)
    for side, idx in (("L", L_WR), ("R", R_WR)):
        text, t = flash[side]
        if now - t < 0.6:
            cv2.putText(frame, text, (px[idx][0] + 10, px[idx][1] - 10),
                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.9, (0, 0, 255), 2)


def level(world):
    """Rotate the skeleton so the torso is vertical, undoing camera pitch and roll."""
    torso = (world[L_SH] + world[R_SH]) / 2 - (world[L_HIP] + world[R_HIP]) / 2
    a, b = torso / (np.linalg.norm(torso) + 1e-6), np.array([0.0, -1.0, 0.0])
    v, c = np.cross(a, b), np.dot(a, b)
    k = np.array([[0, -v[2], v[1]], [v[2], 0, -v[0]], [-v[1], v[0], 0]])
    return world @ (np.eye(3) + k + k @ k / (1 + c)).T


def draw_3d(world, vis, yaw, size=480, scale=250):
    """Orthographic render of the world-space skeleton, rotated by yaw around the vertical axis."""
    canvas = np.zeros((size, size, 3), np.uint8)
    if min(vis[L_HIP], vis[R_HIP]) > 0.5:  # need the hips to find the torso
        world = level(world)
    c, s = np.cos(yaw), np.sin(yaw)
    x = -(world[:, 0] * c + world[:, 2] * s)  # negated to match the mirrored camera view
    px = (np.stack([x, world[:, 1]], axis=1) * scale + [size / 2, size * 0.55]).astype(int)
    for a, b in CONNECTIONS:
        if vis[a] > 0.4 and vis[b] > 0.4:
            cv2.line(canvas, tuple(px[a]), tuple(px[b]), (0, 255, 0), 3)
    for i in (NOSE, L_SH, R_SH, L_EL, R_EL):
        cv2.circle(canvas, tuple(px[i]), 6, (0, 200, 255), -1)
    for i in (L_WR, R_WR):
        cv2.circle(canvas, tuple(px[i]), 10, (0, 0, 255), -1)
    return canvas


def main(on_punch=None, on_states=None, on_frame=None, want_calibrate=None, on_calibrated=None,
         on_features=None, on_draw=None, builtin_punches=True):
    """Run the tracker. Run on its own it only draws; the callbacks let other code react.

    on_punch(kind, side, speed): a punch was recognised. kind is JAB, CROSS, HOOK or UPPERCUT.
    on_states(states): called every frame with the body-state labels active right now (BLOCK, DUCK,
        SLIP LEFT, SLIP RIGHT, GUARD DOWN). It gets an empty list when nobody is in view.
    on_frame(): called every frame; return True to stop the tracker.
    want_calibrate(): called every frame; return True to calibrate now. This lets a hotkey recalibrate
        while another window (the game) has focus. The c key in the camera window always works too.
    on_calibrated(): called after a successful calibration.
    on_features(now, speeds, travel, from_low): the raw numbers the punch decision uses, every frame.
        speeds = [left, right] wrist speed; travel = 2x3 array of (extension, right, up) per hand;
        from_low = [left, right] wrist started below the elbow. It may return a list of (side, kind)
        punches it decided; those are shown on screen and passed to on_punch.
    on_draw(frame): draw extra text on the camera image before it is shown.
    builtin_punches: set False to switch off this file's own punch check, so only the punches
        returned by on_features count (see punch_detector.py).
    """
    ensure_model()
    landmarker = vision.PoseLandmarker.create_from_options(vision.PoseLandmarkerOptions(
        base_options=mp_python.BaseOptions(model_asset_path=MODEL_PATH),
        running_mode=vision.RunningMode.VIDEO,
        min_pose_detection_confidence=0.4,
        min_pose_presence_confidence=0.4,
        min_tracking_confidence=0.4,
    ))
    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)
    if not cap.isOpened():
        raise SystemExit("Could not open webcam")

    smooth_img, smooth_world = Smoother(0.6), Smoother(0.7)
    yaw = 0.0  # 3D view rotation
    cv2.namedWindow("3D skeleton")
    cv2.moveWindow("3D skeleton", 700, 50)  # beside the camera window, not on top of it
    history = deque(maxlen=5)  # (time, wrist-relative-to-shoulder, wrist-below-elbow), ~0.2 s
    baseline = None
    calibrated_at = -10.0  # when the last calibration happened, for the on-screen flash
    last_punch = {"L": 0.0, "R": 0.0}
    flash = {"L": ("", 0.0), "R": ("", 0.0)}
    t0 = time.time()

    failed_reads = 0
    while True:
        ok, frame = cap.read()
        if not ok or frame is None:
            # Some webcams return empty frames for the first moment after opening. Wait before giving up.
            failed_reads += 1
            if failed_reads > 150:  # about 3 seconds of nothing
                break
            time.sleep(0.02)
            continue
        failed_reads = 0
        now = time.time()
        rgb = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        result = landmarker.detect_for_video(
            mp.Image(image_format=mp.ImageFormat.SRGB, data=rgb), int((now - t0) * 1000))
        frame = cv2.flip(frame, 1)  # mirror for display only; image x is flipped to match
        lines = ["no body detected"]

        if result.pose_landmarks:
            lm = result.pose_landmarks[0]
            img = smooth_img(np.array([[1 - p.x, p.y] for p in lm]))
            vis = np.array([p.visibility for p in lm])
            world = smooth_world(np.array([[p.x, p.y, p.z] for p in result.pose_world_landmarks[0]]))
            sw = np.linalg.norm(world[L_SH] - world[R_SH]) + 1e-6

            wrist_below_elbow = world[[L_WR, R_WR], 1] > world[[L_EL, R_EL], 1]  # world y points down
            history.append((now, world[[L_WR, R_WR]] - world[[L_SH, R_SH]], wrist_below_elbow))
            dt = now - history[0][0]
            speeds = [0.0, 0.0]
            if dt > 0:
                delta = (history[-1][1] - history[0][1]) / sw
                travel = punch_travel(delta, history[0][1], history[-1][1], world, sw)
                for i, side in enumerate("LR"):
                    speeds[i] = np.linalg.norm(delta[i]) / dt
                    if builtin_punches and speeds[i] > PUNCH_SPEED and now - last_punch[side] > PUNCH_COOLDOWN:
                        kind = classify_punch(side, travel[i], history[0][2][i])
                        ext, right, up = travel[i]
                        print(f"{side} {kind} speed={speeds[i]:.1f} extension={ext:.2f} right={right:.2f} up={up:.2f} low={history[0][2][i]}")
                        if kind:
                            last_punch[side] = now
                            flash[side] = (f"{kind} {speeds[i]:.1f}", now)
                            if on_punch:
                                on_punch(kind, side, speeds[i])
                if on_features:
                    for side, kind in on_features(now, list(speeds), travel, list(history[0][2])) or ():
                        flash[side] = (kind, now)
                        if on_punch:
                            on_punch(kind, side, speeds["LR".index(side)])

            states = body_state(img, world, sw, baseline)
            if on_states:
                on_states(states)
            lines = [" | ".join(states) or "ok",
                     f"speed L {speeds[0]:.1f}  R {speeds[1]:.1f}"]
            draw(frame, img, vis, flash, now)
            cv2.imshow("3D skeleton", draw_3d(world, vis, yaw))
        else:
            cv2.imshow("3D skeleton", np.zeros((480, 480, 3), np.uint8))
            if on_states:
                on_states([])  # nobody in view: let go of any held keys

        for n, text in enumerate(lines):
            cv2.putText(frame, text, (10, 30 + 30 * n), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.8, (255, 255, 255), 2)
        if baseline is None:
            cv2.putText(frame, "stand in guard, then press C to calibrate", (10, frame.shape[0] - 15),
                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, (0, 255, 255), 2)
        else:
            if now - calibrated_at < 1.5:
                cv2.putText(frame, "CALIBRATED", (10, frame.shape[0] - 45),
                            cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1.0, (0, 255, 0), 3)
            cv2.putText(frame, "C = recalibrate", (10, frame.shape[0] - 15),
                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (200, 200, 200), 1)
        if on_draw:
            on_draw(frame)
        cv2.imshow("Pose", frame)
        if on_frame and on_frame():
            break
        key = cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF
        calibrate = key == ord("c") or bool(want_calibrate and want_calibrate())
        if calibrate and result.pose_landmarks:
            baseline = {"nose": img[NOSE].copy(), "sw": np.linalg.norm(img[L_SH] - img[R_SH])}
            calibrated_at = now
            print("Calibrated")
            if on_calibrated:
                on_calibrated()
        elif calibrate:
            print("Calibration skipped: no body in view")
        elif key in (ord("a"), ord("d")):
            yaw += 0.15 if key == ord("d") else -0.15
        elif key == ord("q"):
            break

    if on_states:
        on_states([])
    cap.release()
    cv2.destroyAllWindows()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	"""Check that the glove is sending good data, one step at a time, and say what to fix if it is not.
2	
3	  python glove_check.py              wait for the real glove on UDP port 5005
4	  python glove_check.py --simulate   try this tool with a fake glove (no hardware)
5	
6	Steps:
7	  1  Hear the glove      any packet arrives at all
8	  2  Data quality        frames arrive intact, at the right rate, with few gaps
9	  3  At rest             hold it still: gravity should read 1 g and rotation near zero
10	  4  Punches             throw a few; each is counted with its impact strength
11	
12	Nothing is pressed or sent to any game.
13	"""
14	import argparse
15	import socket
16	import statistics
17	import sys
18	import threading
19	import time
20	
21	import numpy as np
22	
23	import glove_punch
24	import glove_receiver
25	
26	PORT = glove_receiver.PORT
27	FRAME_LEN = glove_receiver.FRAME_LEN
28	
29	
30	def say(text=""):
31	    print(text, flush=True)
32	
33	
34	def laptop_addresses():
35	    found = set()
36	    try:
37	        probe = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
38	        probe.connect(("203.0.113.1", 9))  # documentation address; connecting a UDP socket sends nothing
39	        found.add(probe.getsockname()[0])
40	        probe.close()
41	    except OSError:
42	        pass
43	    try:
44	        found.update(socket.gethostbyname_ex(socket.gethostname())[2])
45	    except OSError:
46	        pass
47	    return sorted(a for a in found if not a.startswith("127."))
48	
49	
50	def collect(sock, seconds, on_packet=None):
51	    """Receive for `seconds`. Returns a list of (arrival_time, sender_ip, data)."""
52	    packets, end = [], time.time() + seconds
53	    while time.time() < end:
54	        sock.settimeout(max(0.01, min(0.2, end - time.time())))
55	        try:
56	            data, addr = sock.recvfrom(4096)
57	        except socket.timeout:
58	            continue
59	        item = (time.time(), addr[0], data)
60	        packets.append(item)
61	        if on_packet:
62	            on_packet(*item)
63	    return packets
64	
65	
66	def step1_hear(sock, wait_seconds):
67	    say("STEP 1 of 4: listening for the glove on UDP port %d (up to %d s)..." % (PORT, wait_seconds))
68	    say("  Power the glove now. The ESP32 prints 'Connected' on its serial monitor when it joins Wi-Fi.")
69	    end, last_note = time.time() + wait_seconds, time.time()
70	    first = []
71	    while time.time() < end and not first:
72	        first = collect(sock, 1.0)
73	        if not first and time.time() - last_note >= 5:
74	            say("  ... nothing yet (%d s left)" % max(0, end - time.time()))
75	            last_note = time.time()
76	    if first:
77	        senders = sorted({p[1] for p in first})
78	        say("  PASS: heard the glove, from %s" % ", ".join(senders))
79	        return first
80	    say("  FAIL: no packets arrived.")
81	    try:
82	        loop = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
83	        loop.sendto(b"self-test", ("127.0.0.1", PORT))
84	        sock.settimeout(1.0)
85	        sock.recvfrom(64)
86	        say("  This computer's own socket works (a packet sent to itself arrived), so the problem is the")
87	        say("  glove, the Wi-Fi network, or the Windows firewall.")
88	    except OSError as e:
89	        say("  Even a packet sent to itself did not arrive (%s), so something is wrong on this computer." % e)
90	    say("  Check these, most likely first:")
91	    say("   1. Network. The glove and this laptop must be on the SAME Wi-Fi network. This laptop's address(es): %s"
92	        % (", ".join(laptop_addresses()) or "unknown"))
93	    say("      University Wi-Fi (eduroam) will not work: the ESP32 cannot log into it, and it also blocks")
94	    say("      devices from talking to each other. Use a phone hotspot (2.4 GHz band) or a travel router,")
95	    say("      and connect both the laptop and the glove to it.")
96	    say("   2. Firmware settings (config.h): WIFI_SSID and WIFI_PASSWORD must be that network. Set LAPTOP_IP")
97	    say("      to this laptop's address ON THAT NETWORK (leaving it empty uses broadcast, which many networks block).")
98	    say("   3. Windows firewall. The first time Python listens, Windows asks to allow it. Choose 'Allow', and")
99	    say("      tick the box for the network type you are on. Public networks are blocked by default.")
100	    say("   4. The glove itself: open its serial monitor at 115200 baud. It reports 'MPU6050 not found' for a")
101	    say("      wiring problem, and the line 'Sending UDP to <address> port 5005' once it is on Wi-Fi.")
102	    return None
103	
104	
105	def parse(packets, clock_per_sender=None):
106	    """Turn packets into samples. Returns (samples, total_bytes, junk_bytes)."""
107	    samples, total, good = [], 0, 0
108	    for arrival, sender, data in packets:
109	        total += len(data)
110	        clock = None
111	        if clock_per_sender is not None:
112	            clock = clock_per_sender.setdefault(sender, glove_receiver.Clock())
113	        for s in glove_receiver.parse_frames(data):
114	            good += FRAME_LEN
115	            if clock:
116	                clock.stamp(s, arrival)
117	            samples.append(s)
118	    return samples, total, total - good
119	
120	
121	def step2_quality(sock, seconds, expected_hz, check_rate=True):
122	    say("")
123	    say("STEP 2 of 4: checking data quality for %d s..." % seconds)
124	    packets = collect(sock, seconds)
125	    samples, total, junk = parse(packets)
126	    if not samples:
127	        say("  FAIL: %d packets arrived but none held a valid frame. The data is corrupted or in the wrong" % len(packets))
128	        say("  format (are two devices sending to the same port?).")
129	        return False
130	    ok = True
131	    t_us = np.array([s.t_us for s in samples], dtype=np.int64)
132	    steps = np.diff(t_us) & 0xFFFFFFFF
133	    steps = steps[steps < 5_000_000] / 1e6  # seconds between frames; a bigger jump is a reboot
134	    sensor_hz = 1.0 / np.median(steps) if len(steps) else 0.0
135	    nominal = 1.0 / expected_hz
136	    lost = float(np.sum(np.maximum(steps / nominal - 1, 0)[steps > 1.9 * nominal])) if len(steps) else 0.0
137	    loss_pct = 100.0 * lost / max(lost + len(samples), 1)

"""Check that the glove is sending good data, one step at a time, and say what to fix if it is not.

  python glove_check.py              wait for the real glove on UDP port 5005
  python glove_check.py --simulate   try this tool with a fake glove (no hardware)

Steps:
  1  Hear the glove      any packet arrives at all
  2  Data quality        frames arrive intact, at the right rate, with few gaps
  3  At rest             hold it still: gravity should read 1 g and rotation near zero
  4  Punches             throw a few; each is counted with its impact strength

Nothing is pressed or sent to any game.
"""
import argparse
import socket
import statistics
import sys
import threading
import time

import numpy as np

import glove_punch
import glove_receiver

PORT = glove_receiver.PORT
FRAME_LEN = glove_receiver.FRAME_LEN


def say(text=""):
    print(text, flush=True)


def laptop_addresses():
    found = set()
    try:
        probe = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        probe.connect(("203.0.113.1", 9))  # documentation address; connecting a UDP socket sends nothing
        found.add(probe.getsockname()[0])
        probe.close()
    except OSError:
        pass
    try:
        found.update(socket.gethostbyname_ex(socket.gethostname())[2])
    except OSError:
        pass
    return sorted(a for a in found if not a.startswith("127."))


def collect(sock, seconds, on_packet=None):
    """Receive for `seconds`. Returns a list of (arrival_time, sender_ip, data)."""
    packets, end = [], time.time() + seconds
    while time.time() < end:
        sock.settimeout(max(0.01, min(0.2, end - time.time())))
        try:
            data, addr = sock.recvfrom(4096)
        except socket.timeout:
            continue
        item = (time.time(), addr[0], data)
        packets.append(item)
        if on_packet:
            on_packet(*item)
    return packets


def step1_hear(sock, wait_seconds):
    say("STEP 1 of 4: listening for the glove on UDP port %d (up to %d s)..." % (PORT, wait_seconds))
    say("  Power the glove now. The ESP32 prints 'Connected' on its serial monitor when it joins Wi-Fi.")
    end, last_note = time.time() + wait_seconds, time.time()
    first = []
    while time.time() < end and not first:
        first = collect(sock, 1.0)
        if not first and time.time() - last_note >= 5:
            say("  ... nothing yet (%d s left)" % max(0, end - time.time()))
            last_note = time.time()
    if first:
        senders = sorted({p[1] for p in first})
        say("  PASS: heard the glove, from %s" % ", ".join(senders))
        return first
    say("  FAIL: no packets arrived.")
    try:
        loop = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        loop.sendto(b"self-test", ("127.0.0.1", PORT))
        sock.settimeout(1.0)
        sock.recvfrom(64)
        say("  This computer's own socket works (a packet sent to itself arrived), so the problem is the")
        say("  glove, the Wi-Fi network, or the Windows firewall.")
    except OSError as e:
        say("  Even a packet sent to itself did not arrive (%s), so something is wrong on this computer." % e)
    say("  Check these, most likely first:")
    say("   1. Network. The glove and this laptop must be on the SAME Wi-Fi network. This laptop's address(es): %s"
        % (", ".join(laptop_addresses()) or "unknown"))
    say("      University Wi-Fi (eduroam) will not work: the ESP32 cannot log into it, and it also blocks")
    say("      devices from talking to each other. Use a phone hotspot (2.4 GHz band) or a travel router,")
    say("      and connect both the laptop and the glove to it.")
    say("   2. Firmware settings (config.h): WIFI_SSID and WIFI_PASSWORD must be that network. Set LAPTOP_IP")
    say("      to this laptop's address ON THAT NETWORK (leaving it empty uses broadcast, which many networks block).")
    say("   3. Windows firewall. The first time Python listens, Windows asks to allow it. Choose 'Allow', and")
    say("      tick the box for the network type you are on. Public networks are blocked by default.")
    say("   4. The glove itself: open its serial monitor at 115200 baud. It reports 'MPU6050 not found' for a")
    say("      wiring problem, and the line 'Sending UDP to <address> port 5005' once it is on Wi-Fi.")
    return None


def parse(packets, clock_per_sender=None):
    """Turn packets into samples. Returns (samples, total_bytes, junk_bytes)."""
    samples, total, good = [], 0, 0
    for arrival, sender, data in packets:
        total += len(data)
        clock = None
        if clock_per_sender is not None:
            clock = clock_per_sender.setdefault(sender, glove_receiver.Clock())
        for s in glove_receiver.parse_frames(data):
            good += FRAME_LEN
            if clock:
                clock.stamp(s, arrival)
            samples.append(s)
    return samples, total, total - good


def step2_quality(sock, seconds, expected_hz, check_rate=True):
    say("")
    say("STEP 2 of 4: checking data quality for %d s..." % seconds)
    packets = collect(sock, seconds)
    samples, total, junk = parse(packets)
    if not samples:
        say("  FAIL: %d packets arrived but none held a valid frame. The data is corrupted or in the wrong" % len(packets))
        say("  format (are two devices sending to the same port?).")
        return False
    ok = True
    t_us = np.array([s.t_us for s in samples], dtype=np.int64)
    steps = np.diff(t_us) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    steps = steps[steps < 5_000_000] / 1e6  # seconds between frames; a bigger jump is a reboot
    sensor_hz = 1.0 / np.median(steps) if len(steps) else 0.0
    nominal = 1.0 / expected_hz
    lost = float(np.sum(np.maximum(steps / nominal - 1, 0)[steps > 1.9 * nominal])) if len(steps) else 0.0
    loss_pct = 100.0 * lost / max(lost + len(samples), 1)
    gaps = int(np.sum(steps > 0.05)) if len(steps) else 0
    say("  packets %d | frames %d (%.0f per second) | sensor rate from its own clock: %.0f Hz (expect about %d)"
        % (len(packets), len(samples), len(samples) / seconds, sensor_hz, expected_hz))
    say("  junk bytes: %d of %d | estimated lost frames: %.1f%% | gaps longer than 50 ms: %d"
        % (junk, total, loss_pct, gaps))
    if check_rate and abs(sensor_hz - expected_hz) > 0.15 * expected_hz:
        say("  PROBLEM: the sensor is not sampling at the expected rate. Compare with the 'Sensor ... Hz' line"
            " on the ESP32 serial monitor.")
        ok = False
    if junk > 0.02 * total:
        say("  PROBLEM: more than 2%% of the bytes are not valid frames. Check for another device sending to port %d." % PORT)
        ok = False
    if check_rate and (loss_pct > 10 or gaps > 3):
        say("  PROBLEM: the Wi-Fi link is dropping data. Move closer, use a 2.4 GHz hotspot, and avoid a busy network.")
        ok = False
    say("  " + ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL") + ": data quality")
    return ok


def step3_rest(sock, seconds):
    say("")
    say("STEP 3 of 4: HOLD THE GLOVE STILL for %d s (rest it on the table)..." % seconds)
    samples, _, _ = parse(collect(sock, seconds))
    if len(samples) < 20:
        say("  FAIL: not enough data.")
        return False
    accel = np.array([float(np.linalg.norm(s.accel)) for s in samples])
    gyro = np.array([float(np.linalg.norm(s.gyro)) for s in samples])
    a, g = statistics.median(accel), statistics.median(gyro)
    a_sd = 1.4826 * float(np.median(np.abs(accel - a)))  # typical noise, not thrown by a few bumps
    moving = 100.0 * float(np.mean(np.abs(accel - 1.0) > 0.5))
    say("  gravity reads %.2f g (should be 1.00) with noise %.3f g | rotation at rest %.1f deg/s (should be under 5)"
        % (a, a_sd, g))
    if moving > 10:
        say("  NOTE: the glove moved noticeably during %.0f%% of this step. Rest it on the table for a cleaner reading."
            % moving)
    ok = True
    if 0.9 <= a <= 1.1:
        pass
    elif 6.5 <= a <= 9.5:
        say("  PROBLEM: gravity reads about 8 g. The sensor has reset to its +-2 g range while the code assumes")
        say("  +-16 g. Power-cycle the glove (the firmware also re-configures it every quarter of a second).")
        ok = False
    elif a < 0.3:
        say("  PROBLEM: the accelerometer reads almost zero. The sensor may be disconnected or not awake.")
        ok = False
    else:
        say("  PROBLEM: gravity should read 1 g. Check the sensor range settings in the firmware and in glove_receiver.py.")
        ok = False
    if a_sd > 0.1:
        say("  PROBLEM: the reading is noisy at rest (%.3f g). Was the glove really still?" % a_sd)
        ok = False
    if g > 5:
        say("  NOTE: the gyroscope reads %.1f deg/s at rest. A small offset is normal; a large one needs"
            " calibration or a re-check that the glove was still." % g)
    say("  " + ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL") + ": at rest")
    return ok


def step4_punches(sock, wanted, seconds):
    say("")
    say("STEP 4 of 4: THROW %d PUNCHES with the glove on (pause between them). Listening for %d s..." % (wanted, seconds))
    clocks, detectors, found = {}, {}, []
    peak_any = [0.0]

    def handle(arrival, sender, data):
        clock = clocks.setdefault(sender, glove_receiver.Clock())
        det = detectors.setdefault(sender, glove_punch.PunchDetector())
        for s in glove_receiver.parse_frames(data):
            clock.stamp(s, arrival)
            peak_any[0] = max(peak_any[0], abs(float(np.linalg.norm(s.accel)) - 1.0))
            punch = det.update(s)
            if punch:
                found.append(punch)
                say("  punch %d: impact %.1f g, lasted %d ms" % (len(found), punch.peak_g, round(punch.duration * 1000)))

    end = time.time() + seconds
    while time.time() < end and len(found) < wanted:
        collect(sock, min(0.5, max(0.01, end - time.time())), handle)
    say("  strongest movement seen: %.1f g beyond gravity (a punch is counted above %.1f g)"
        % (peak_any[0], glove_punch.START_G))
    if len(found) >= wanted:
        say("  PASS: %d punches detected" % len(found))
        return True
    say("  FAIL: %d of %d punches detected." % (len(found), wanted))
    if peak_any[0] < glove_punch.START_G:
        say("  Your hardest movement stayed below the trigger. If you were punching hard, lower START_G in"
            " glove_punch.py (try %.1f)." % max(1.0, peak_any[0] * 0.7))
    else:
        say("  The glove felt hard movements but they did not count as punches. Raise END_G or lower COOLDOWN in glove_punch.py.")
    return False


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use a fake glove to try this tool")
    parser.add_argument("--wait", type=int, default=45, help="seconds to wait for the glove (step 1)")
    parser.add_argument("--hz", type=int, default=500, help="sensor rate the firmware should produce")
    parser.add_argument("--punches", type=int, default=5, help="punches to throw in step 4")
    parser.add_argument("--punch-seconds", type=int, default=30)
    parser.add_argument("--until", type=int, default=4, choices=[1, 2, 3, 4],
                        help="stop after this step (steps 3 and 4 need you to hold still / punch)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    try:
        sock.bind(("0.0.0.0", PORT))
    except OSError as e:
        say("Cannot listen on UDP port %d: %s" % (PORT, e))
        say("Another program (such as controller.py --glove) is probably using it. Close it and try again.")
        return 1
    if args.simulate:
        say("SIMULATION: a fake 200 Hz glove that punches every 1.5 s. Real hardware is not involved.")
        threading.Thread(target=glove_receiver.simulate, daemon=True).start()
        args.hz = 200
    results = {}
    try:
        if step1_hear(sock, 10 if args.simulate else args.wait) is None:
            return 1
        if args.until >= 2:
            results["data quality"] = step2_quality(sock, 5, args.hz, check_rate=not args.simulate)
        if args.until >= 3:
            results["at rest"] = step3_rest(sock, 4)
        if args.until >= 4:
            results["punches"] = step4_punches(sock, args.punches, args.punch_seconds)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        say("\nStopped.")
        return 1
    say("")
    say("SUMMARY: " + " | ".join("%s: %s" % (k, "ok" if v else "PROBLEM") for k, v in results.items()))
    return 0 if all(results.values()) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	"""Play a game with your body: camera punches and poses become key presses.
2	
3	  python controller.py          dry run: prints the keys it would press, presses nothing
4	  python controller.py --live   really presses keys in whichever window has focus
5	
6	Hotkeys work from any window, so you can click the game and still control this:
7	  F7  calibrate or recalibrate (stand in your guard first; you hear a beep when it worked)
8	  F8  turn key output on or off (with --live it starts OFF, so nothing is typed by accident)
9	  F9  quit
10	In the camera window: c = calibrate, a/d = rotate the 3D view, q = quit.
11	"""
12	import argparse
13	import ctypes
14	import os
15	import sys
16	
17	import game_input
18	import punch_detector
19	
20	VK_F7, VK_F8, VK_F9 = 0x76, 0x77, 0x78
21	
22	
23	def beep():
24	    """A short system sound, so you know something happened while you are looking at the game."""
25	    if sys.platform == "win32":
26	        ctypes.windll.user32.MessageBeep(0)
27	
28	
29	def key_is_down(vk):
30	    """True while a key is held, whichever window has focus (Windows only)."""
31	    if sys.platform != "win32":
32	        return False
33	    return bool(ctypes.windll.user32.GetAsyncKeyState(vk) & 0x8000)
34	
35	
36	class Hotkeys:
37	    """Reports a key once when it goes down, not every frame while it is held."""
38	
39	    def __init__(self, read=key_is_down):
40	        self.read, self.was_down = read, {}
41	
42	    def pressed(self, vk):
43	        down = self.read(vk)
44	        fired = down and not self.was_down.get(vk, False)
45	        self.was_down[vk] = down
46	        return fired
47	
48	
49	def make_callbacks(game, hotkeys, log=print, glove=None, sound=beep, detector=None):
50	    """Build the callbacks for pose_tracker.main(), as a dict of keyword arguments.
51	
52	    Kept separate from main() so it can be tested without a camera.
53	    detector is a punch_detector.PunchDetector; pass False to use pose_tracker's own punch check.
54	
55	    glove is an optional glove_punch.GlovePunches. When given, a camera punch only counts if that
56	    hand's glove also felt one. A hand with no glove connected is never blocked.
57	    """
58	    last_states = []
59	
60	    def on_punch(kind, side, speed):
61	        if glove is not None:
62	            glove.poll()
63	            if not glove.confirms(side):
64	                log(f"{side} {kind} ignored (the {side} glove felt no punch)")
65	                return
66	        if not game.enabled:
67	            log(f"{side} {kind} (output OFF, press F8)")
68	        elif game.punch(kind):
69	            log(f"{side} {kind} -> {game.mapping.taps[kind.upper()]}")
70	        else:
71	            log(f"{side} {kind} (no key mapped, or key already down)")
72	
73	    def on_states(states):
74	        nonlocal last_states
75	        game.set_states(states)
76	        if list(states) != last_states and game.enabled:
77	            log("state: " + (", ".join(states) or "none"))
78	        last_states = list(states)
79	
80	    def on_frame():
81	        if glove is not None:
82	            glove.poll()
83	        if hotkeys.pressed(VK_F8):
84	            game.set_enabled(not game.enabled)
85	            log("key output " + ("ON" if game.enabled else "OFF"))
86	        return hotkeys.pressed(VK_F9)
87	
88	    def want_calibrate():
89	        return hotkeys.pressed(VK_F7)
90	
91	    def on_calibrated():
92	        log("calibrated")
93	        sound()
94	
95	    callbacks = dict(on_punch=on_punch, on_states=on_states, on_frame=on_frame,
96	                     want_calibrate=want_calibrate, on_calibrated=on_calibrated)
97	    if detector is not False:
98	        detector = detector or punch_detector.PunchDetector()
99	        callbacks["on_features"] = detector.update
100	        callbacks["builtin_punches"] = False
101	    return callbacks

"""Play a game with your body: camera punches and poses become key presses.

  python controller.py          dry run: prints the keys it would press, presses nothing
  python controller.py --live   really presses keys in whichever window has focus

Hotkeys work from any window, so you can click the game and still control this:
  F7  calibrate or recalibrate (stand in your guard first; you hear a beep when it worked)
  F8  turn key output on or off (with --live it starts OFF, so nothing is typed by accident)
  F9  quit
In the camera window: c = calibrate, a/d = rotate the 3D view, q = quit.
"""
import argparse
import ctypes
import os
import sys

import game_input
import punch_detector

VK_F7, VK_F8, VK_F9 = 0x76, 0x77, 0x78


def beep():
    """A short system sound, so you know something happened while you are looking at the game."""
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        ctypes.windll.user32.MessageBeep(0)


def key_is_down(vk):
    """True while a key is held, whichever window has focus (Windows only)."""
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        return False
    return bool(ctypes.windll.user32.GetAsyncKeyState(vk) & 0x8000)


class Hotkeys:
    """Reports a key once when it goes down, not every frame while it is held."""

    def __init__(self, read=key_is_down):
        self.read, self.was_down = read, {}

    def pressed(self, vk):
        down = self.read(vk)
        fired = down and not self.was_down.get(vk, False)
        self.was_down[vk] = down
        return fired


def make_callbacks(game, hotkeys, log=print, glove=None, sound=beep, detector=None):
    """Build the callbacks for pose_tracker.main(), as a dict of keyword arguments.

    Kept separate from main() so it can be tested without a camera.
    detector is a punch_detector.PunchDetector; pass False to use pose_tracker's own punch check.

    glove is an optional glove_punch.GlovePunches. When given, a camera punch only counts if that
    hand's glove also felt one. A hand with no glove connected is never blocked.
    """
    last_states = []

    def on_punch(kind, side, speed):
        if glove is not None:
            glove.poll()
            if not glove.confirms(side):
                log(f"{side} {kind} ignored (the {side} glove felt no punch)")
                return
        if not game.enabled:
            log(f"{side} {kind} (output OFF, press F8)")
        elif game.punch(kind):
            log(f"{side} {kind} -> {game.mapping.taps[kind.upper()]}")
        else:
            log(f"{side} {kind} (no key mapped, or key already down)")

    def on_states(states):
        nonlocal last_states
        game.set_states(states)
        if list(states) != last_states and game.enabled:
            log("state: " + (", ".join(states) or "none"))
        last_states = list(states)

    def on_frame():
        if glove is not None:
            glove.poll()
        if hotkeys.pressed(VK_F8):
            game.set_enabled(not game.enabled)
            log("key output " + ("ON" if game.enabled else "OFF"))
        return hotkeys.pressed(VK_F9)

    def want_calibrate():
        return hotkeys.pressed(VK_F7)

    def on_calibrated():
        log("calibrated")
        sound()

    callbacks = dict(on_punch=on_punch, on_states=on_states, on_frame=on_frame,
                     want_calibrate=want_calibrate, on_calibrated=on_calibrated)
    if detector is not False:
        detector = detector or punch_detector.PunchDetector()
        callbacks["on_features"] = detector.update
        callbacks["builtin_punches"] = False
    return callbacks


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--mapping", default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "mappings", "browser_boxing.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--live", action="store_true", help="really press keys (default: only print them)")
    parser.add_argument("--glove", action="store_true",
                        help="listen for the glove on UDP port 5005 and only accept punches the glove also felt")
    parser.add_argument("--builtin-punches", action="store_true",
                        help="use pose_tracker's original punch check instead of punch_detector.py")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate-glove", action="store_true",
                        help="like --glove, but with a fake glove that punches every 1.5 s (for testing)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    mapping = game_input.Mapping.load(args.mapping)
    keyboard = game_input.SendInputKeyboard() if args.live else game_input.DryRunKeyboard()
    game = game_input.GameInput(mapping, keyboard)
    game.set_enabled(not args.live)  # a dry run is harmless, so it starts on; live starts off

    print(f"Game: {mapping.game}")
    print("LIVE: keys go to the focused window." if args.live else "Dry run: nothing is pressed.")
    print(f"Key output is {'ON' if game.enabled else 'OFF'}. F7 calibrates, F8 toggles output, F9 quits.")
    print("Stand in your guard in front of the camera and press F7 to calibrate (any time, from any window).")
    if not args.builtin_punches:
        print("Camera punches: HOOK and UPPERCUT are detected. Straight punches (jab, cross) are not: a webcam")
        print("facing you cannot see them. Use a glove for those, or press the jab/cross keys by hand.")

    glove = None
    if args.glove or args.simulate_glove:
        import threading
        import glove_punch
        import glove_receiver
        receiver = glove_receiver.GloveReceiver()
        if args.simulate_glove:
            threading.Thread(target=glove_receiver.simulate, daemon=True).start()
        glove = glove_punch.GlovePunches(receiver)
        print("Glove: listening on UDP port 5005. Camera punches need a matching glove punch.")

    import pose_tracker  # imported here so the rest of this file works without OpenCV or MediaPipe
    callbacks = make_callbacks(game, Hotkeys(), glove=glove, detector=False if args.builtin_punches else None)
    try:
        pose_tracker.main(**callbacks)
    finally:
        game.close()  # lets go of every key


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Two kinds of key output:
  tap  - a punch. The key is pressed, then released a few milliseconds later. Games read the key
         state once per frame, so a press that is released instantly can be missed.
  hold - a body state (block, duck, slip). The key stays down while the state lasts.

Keys are sent as hardware scan codes with the Windows SendInput call. Browsers and DirectInput games
accept these; many games ignore the plain virtual-key events that most keyboard libraries send.

The event names are the labels pose_tracker.py already produces: JAB, CROSS, HOOK, UPPERCUT for
punches and BLOCK, DUCK, SLIP LEFT, SLIP RIGHT, GUARD DOWN for body states. A mapping file (see
mappings/) says which key each one presses.

Run `python game_input.py` for a dry run that only prints. `--live` really presses keys.
"""
import argparse
import atexit
import ctypes
import json
import os
import sys
import threading
import time

# Hardware scan codes (set 1). Arrow keys are "extended" keys and need the extended flag.
SCAN_CODES = {
    **dict(zip("qwertyuiop", range(0x10, 0x1A))),
    **dict(zip("asdfghjkl", range(0x1E, 0x27))),
    **dict(zip("zxcvbnm", range(0x2C, 0x33))),
    **dict(zip("1234567890", range(0x02, 0x0C))),
    "space": 0x39, "enter": 0x1C, "esc": 0x01, "tab": 0x0F,
    "shift": 0x2A, "ctrl": 0x1D, "alt": 0x38,
    "comma": 0x33, "period": 0x34, "semicolon": 0x27,
    "up": 0x48, "down": 0x50, "left": 0x4B, "right": 0x4D,
}
EXTENDED_KEYS = {"up", "down", "left", "right"}

KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY, KEYEVENTF_KEYUP, KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE = 0x0001, 0x0002, 0x0008
INPUT_KEYBOARD = 1

if sys.platform == "win32":
    from ctypes import wintypes

    ULONG_PTR = ctypes.c_ulonglong if ctypes.sizeof(ctypes.c_void_p) == 8 else ctypes.c_ulong

    class _KeyBdInput(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("wVk", wintypes.WORD), ("wScan", wintypes.WORD), ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("time", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwExtraInfo", ULONG_PTR)]

    class _MouseInput(ctypes.Structure):  # unused, but it sets the size of the INPUT union
        _fields_ = [("dx", wintypes.LONG), ("dy", wintypes.LONG), ("mouseData", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD), ("time", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwExtraInfo", ULONG_PTR)]

        _fields_ = [("uMsg", wintypes.DWORD), ("wParamL", wintypes.WORD), ("wParamH", wintypes.WORD)]

        _fields_ = [("ki", _KeyBdInput), ("mi", _MouseInput), ("hi", _HardwareInput)]

        _fields_ = [("type", wintypes.DWORD), ("u", _InputUnion)]

    _user32.SendInput.argtypes = (wintypes.UINT, ctypes.POINTER(_Input), ctypes.c_int)

    key = key.lower()

    def __init__(self):

    def handler(event):
        keyboard.release_all()
        return False  # carry on with Windows' normal handling, which ends the program

    keyboard._console_handler = handler_type(handler)  # keep a reference so it is not garbage collected
    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    kernel32.SetConsoleCtrlHandler.argtypes = (handler_type, wintypes.BOOL)
    kernel32.SetConsoleCtrlHandler.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    if not kernel32.SetConsoleCtrlHandler(keyboard._console_handler, True):
        raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())


class SendInputKeyboard(Keyboard):
    """Presses real keys on Windows. Input goes to whichever window has focus."""

    def __init__(self):
        if sys.platform != "win32":
            raise OSError("live key presses are only supported on Windows")
        super().__init__()
        release_keys_when_console_ends(self)

    def _send(self, key, is_down):
        flags = KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE
        if key in EXTENDED_KEYS:
            flags |= KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY
        if not is_down:
            flags |= KEYEVENTF_KEYUP
        event = _Input(type=INPUT_KEYBOARD, u=_InputUnion(ki=_KeyBdInput(0, SCAN_CODES[key], flags, 0, 0)))
        if _user32.SendInput(1, ctypes.byref(event), ctypes.sizeof(event)) != 1:
            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())

    """Which key each event presses. Loaded from a JSON file in mappings/."""

    def __init__(self, data):
        self.game = data.get("game", "")
        self.tap_hold = data.get("tap_hold_ms", 50) / 1000
        self.taps = {name.upper(): check_key(key) for name, key in data.get("taps", {}).items()}
        self.holds = {name.upper(): check_key(key) for name, key in data.get("holds", {}).items()}

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return cls(json.load(f))

    """Call punch() when a punch lands and set_states() every frame with the current body states."""

    def __init__(self, mapping, keyboard):
        self.mapping, self.keyboard = mapping, keyboard
        self.enabled = True
        self._state_keys = set()  # keys currently held because of a body state
        atexit.register(self.close)  # normal exit or an uncaught error; a hard kill can still leave keys down

    def punch(self, kind):
        """Tap the key mapped to this punch. Returns True if a key was sent."""
        key = self.mapping.taps.get(kind.upper())
        if key is None or not self.enabled or key in self.keyboard.down:
            return False
        self.keyboard.press(key)
        timer = threading.Timer(self.mapping.tap_hold, self.keyboard.release, (key,))
        timer.daemon = True
        timer.start()
        return True

    def set_states(self, states):
        """states = the labels active right now, e.g. {"BLOCK", "SLIP LEFT"}. Keys follow the changes."""
        wanted = set()
        if self.enabled:
            wanted = {self.mapping.holds[s.upper()] for s in states if s.upper() in self.mapping.holds}
        for key in self._state_keys - wanted:
            self.keyboard.release(key)
        for key in wanted - self._state_keys:
            self.keyboard.press(key)
        self._state_keys = wanted

    def set_enabled(self, on):
        """Switch key output on or off. Turning it off lets go of every key."""
        self.enabled = on
        if not on:
            self.set_states(())
            self.keyboard.release_all()

    def close(self):
        self.set_enabled(False)

    for kind, key in game_input.mapping.taps.items():
        print(f"  punch {kind} -> tap {key}")
        game_input.punch(kind)
        time.sleep(0.4)
    for state, key in game_input.mapping.holds.items():
        print(f"  state {state} -> hold {key} for 0.6 s")
        game_input.set_states({state})
        time.sleep(0.6)
        game_input.set_states(())
        time.sleep(0.2)

    parser.add_argument("--mapping", default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "mappings", "browser_boxing.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--live", action="store_true", help="really press keys (default: only print them)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

        for n in range(5, 0, -1):

            time.sleep(1)
        keyboard = SendInputKeyboard()
    else:
        print("Dry run: printing keys only. Use --live to press them.")
        keyboard = DryRunKeyboard()
    demo(GameInput(mapping, keyboard))
    print("Done.")

"""Score punch-detection settings against a recorded tune_punches.py session, with no camera needed.

  python replay_punches.py                      newest session, new detector with default settings
  python replay_punches.py --old                what the original pose_tracker check did in that session
  python replay_punches.py --set start_speed=6 min_up=1.0

A punch counts as found if the right hand and kind fired between its beep and the next beep (people
react about a second after the beep). Anything else that fires is a mistake.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import glob
import os
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict

import punch_detector

NUMERIC = {"t", "rep", "spd_L", "spd_R", "ext_L", "right_L", "up_L", "low_L",
           "ext_R", "right_R", "up_R", "low_R"}


def load(path):
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(path)))
    for r in rows:
        for k in NUMERIC:
            r[k] = float(r[k])
    return rows


def beeps(rows):
    """[(time, kind, hand, rep)] for each GO window start."""
    out, seen = [], None
    for r in rows:
        key = (r["kind"], r["hand"], int(r["rep"])) if r["phase"] == "go" else None
        if key and key != seen:
            out.append((r["t"], *key))
        seen = key if key else seen
    return out


def new_events(rows, settings):
    det = punch_detector.PunchDetector(settings)
    events = []
    for r in rows:
        speeds = [r["spd_L"], r["spd_R"]]
        travel = [[r["ext_L"], r["right_L"], r["up_L"]], [r["ext_R"], r["right_R"], r["up_R"]]]
        low = [bool(r["low_L"]), bool(r["low_R"])]
        for side, kind in det.update(r["t"], speeds, travel, low):
            events.append((r["t"], side, kind))
    return events


def old_events(rows):
    return [(r["t"], r["fired"].split(":")[0], r["fired"].split(":")[1]) for r in rows if r["fired"]]


def score(rows, events, quiet=True):
    marks = beeps(rows)
    window = 2.45  # seconds after a beep that still belong to it
    hits = OrderedDict()
    for t, kind, hand, rep in marks:
        hits.setdefault((kind, hand), []).append(
            [e for e in events if t <= e[0] < t + window])
    total = Counter()
    print(f"{'punch':10}{'hand':5}{'found':>7}{'doubled':>9}{'wrong kind/hand':>18}")
    for (kind, hand), windows in hits.items():
        if kind == "NONE":
            n = sum(len(w) for w in windows)
            print(f"{'(no punch)':10}{'':5}{'':>7}{'':>9}{n:>14} fires")
            total["wrong"] += n
            continue
        found = sum(any(e[1] == hand and e[2] == kind for e in w) for w in windows)
        doubled = sum(sum(e[1] == hand and e[2] == kind for e in w) > 1 for w in windows)
        wrong = sum(sum(not (e[1] == hand and e[2] == kind) for e in w) for w in windows)
        print(f"{kind:10}{hand:5}{found:>5}/{len(windows)}{doubled:>9}{wrong:>18}")
        total["found"] += found
        total["wrong"] += wrong
        total["doubled"] += doubled
        total["reps"] += len(windows)
    first, last = marks[0][0], marks[-1][0] + window
    quiet_fires = [e for e in events if e[0] < first or e[0] >= last or
                   rows[min(range(len(rows)), key=lambda i: abs(rows[i]["t"] - e[0]))]["phase"] in ("ready", "announce")]
    print(f"fires while standing still (before/between blocks): {len(quiet_fires)}")
    print(f"TOTAL found {total['found']}/{total['reps']}, doubled {total['doubled']}, "
          f"wrong or extra {total['wrong']}, while still {len(quiet_fires)}")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("file", nargs="?", help="session csv (default: the newest in tuning_data/)")
    parser.add_argument("--old", action="store_true", help="score what pose_tracker's built-in check fired")
    parser.add_argument("--set", nargs="*", default=[], metavar="NAME=VALUE", help="override detector settings")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    path = args.file or sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                                                      "tuning_data", "session_*.csv")))[-1]
    rows = load(path)
    print(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: {len(rows)} frames, {rows[-1]['t']:.0f} s")
    if args.old:
        score(rows, old_events(rows))
        return
    settings = punch_detector.Settings()
    for item in args.set:
        name, value = item.split("=")
        setattr(settings, name, None if value == "None" else float(value))
    print("settings:", settings)
    score(rows, new_events(rows, settings))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Detect punches from glove motion-sensor data, and use them to confirm the camera's punches.

A punch is a short, hard burst of acceleration. We measure how far the total acceleration is from
1 g (gravity), so it does not matter how the glove is tilted. The burst starts when that crosses
START_G and ends when it falls back under END_G. The sensor reports about 200 times a second, far more
often than the camera sees frames, so the glove gives a precise time and a real impact strength.

The glove cannot tell a jab from a hook, so it never chooses the key. The camera does that. The glove
only answers "did this hand really punch just now?", which filters out the camera mistaking a wave
or a reach for a punch.

These numbers are starting points taken from the simulator. Tune them against the real glove.
"""
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

START_G = 3.0         # acceleration beyond gravity that starts a punch
END_G = 1.5           # the punch is over when it falls back below this
COOLDOWN = 0.25       # seconds before the same glove can start another punch
MAX_DURATION = 0.4    # a burst longer than this is reported anyway (shaking, not one punch)


@dataclass
class Punch:
    t: float          # when it started, on the laptop clock
    peak_g: float     # hardest acceleration beyond gravity, in g
    duration: float   # seconds


class PunchDetector:
    """Feed it one glove's samples in order. update() returns a Punch when one has just finished."""

    def __init__(self, start_g=START_G, end_g=END_G, cooldown=COOLDOWN, max_duration=MAX_DURATION):
        self.start_g, self.end_g = start_g, end_g
        self.cooldown, self.max_duration = cooldown, max_duration
        self.active, self.start_t, self.peak, self.last_end = False, 0.0, 0.0, -1e9

    def update(self, sample):
        beyond_gravity = abs(float(np.linalg.norm(sample.accel)) - 1.0)
        if not self.active:
            if beyond_gravity >= self.start_g and sample.t - self.last_end >= self.cooldown:
                self.active, self.start_t, self.peak = True, sample.t, beyond_gravity
            return None
        self.peak = max(self.peak, beyond_gravity)
        if beyond_gravity < self.end_g or sample.t - self.start_t >= self.max_duration:
            self.active, self.last_end = False, sample.t
            return Punch(self.start_t, self.peak, sample.t - self.start_t)
        return None


class GlovePunches:
    """Watches every glove a GloveReceiver hears and remembers each one's latest punch."""

    def __init__(self, receiver, **detector_settings):
        self.receiver, self.settings = receiver, detector_settings
        self.detectors, self.seen_t, self.last = {}, {}, {}

    def poll(self):
        """Run any new samples through the detectors. Returns a list of (glove, Punch)."""
        found = []
        for glove, buffer in list(self.receiver.samples.items()):
            detector = self.detectors.setdefault(glove, PunchDetector(**self.settings))
            seen = self.seen_t.get(glove, -1.0)
            samples = list(buffer)
            if samples and samples[-1].t < seen - 5:  # the glove rebooted and its clock restarted
                seen = -1.0
            for sample in samples:
                if sample.t > seen:
                    seen = sample.t
                    punch = detector.update(sample)
                    if punch:
                        self.last[glove] = punch
                        found.append((glove, punch))
            self.seen_t[glove] = seen
        return found

    def confirms(self, glove, within=0.6, now=None):
        """True if this hand punched in the last `within` seconds.

        A hand with no glove (nothing heard from it) is never blocked, so a single glove still works.
        """
        if glove not in self.receiver.samples:
            return True
        detector = self.detectors.get(glove)
        if detector is not None and detector.active:
            return True  # a punch is happening right now and has not finished yet
        punch = self.last.get(glove)
        now = time.time() if now is None else now
        return punch is not None and -0.1 <= now - punch.t <= within

"""Record a guided punching session so the punch settings can be tuned to how you really move.

  python tune_punches.py

Stand back so your head and both hands are in view, hands up in guard. The camera window shows what
to do. A beep marks the start of each punch. Throw each punch once per beep, then return to guard.
It takes about 2.5 minutes. Nothing is pressed or sent to any game. The measurements are saved to
tuning_data/session_<time>.csv, one row per camera frame.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import ctypes
import os
import sys
import time

import cv2

import pose_tracker

HAND = {"L": "LEFT", "R": "RIGHT"}

# (kind, hand, what to do, repetitions)
BLOCKS = [
    ("JAB", "L", "LEFT hand JAB: punch straight at the camera", 6),
    ("CROSS", "R", "RIGHT hand CROSS: punch straight at the camera", 6),
    ("HOOK", "L", "LEFT hand HOOK: swing in a curve toward the middle", 6),
    ("HOOK", "R", "RIGHT hand HOOK: swing in a curve toward the middle", 6),
    ("UPPERCUT", "L", "LEFT hand UPPERCUT: scoop up from low", 6),
    ("UPPERCUT", "R", "RIGHT hand UPPERCUT: scoop up from low", 6),
    ("NONE", "-", "NO PUNCHES: wave, reach, shift about, stay loose", 6),
]
GO, REST = 1.3, 1.2  # seconds


def build_timeline(ready_seconds=8.0):
    """List of (start, end, phase, kind, hand, rep, title, subtitle)."""
    segs, t = [], 0.0

    def add(duration, phase, kind, hand, rep, title, subtitle=""):
        nonlocal t
        segs.append((t, t + duration, phase, kind, hand, rep, title, subtitle))
        t += duration

    add(ready_seconds, "ready", "", "", 0, "GET READY", "Hands up in guard. Head and both hands in view.")
    for kind, hand, what, reps in BLOCKS:
        add(4.0, "announce", kind, hand, 0, "NEXT", what)
        for rep in range(1, reps + 1):
            add(REST, "rest", kind, hand, rep, "guard", f"{kind} {rep} of {reps} coming")
            title = "MOVE FREELY" if kind == "NONE" else f"{HAND[hand]} {kind}!"
            add(GO, "go", kind, hand, rep, title, f"{rep} of {reps}")
    add(2.0, "done", "", "", 0, "DONE", "Saving...")
    return segs


def beep():
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        ctypes.windll.user32.MessageBeep(0)


class Session:
    COLUMNS = ["t", "phase", "kind", "hand", "rep", "fired", "spd_L", "spd_R",
               "ext_L", "right_L", "up_L", "low_L", "ext_R", "right_R", "up_R", "low_R"]

    def __init__(self, timeline, max_seconds=None):
        self.timeline = timeline
        self.end = timeline[-1][1] if max_seconds is None else min(max_seconds, timeline[-1][1])
        self.t0 = None  # starts with the first video frame, after the camera and model have warmed up
        self.rows, self.fired, self.last_go = [], "", None

    def now(self):
        return 0.0 if self.t0 is None else time.time() - self.t0

    def segment(self, t):
        for seg in self.timeline:
            if seg[0] <= t < seg[1]:
                return seg
        return self.timeline[-1]

    # --- callbacks for pose_tracker.main ---
    def on_punch(self, kind, side, speed):
        self.fired = f"{side}:{kind}"

    def on_features(self, now, speeds, travel, from_low):
        seg = self.segment(self.now())
        self.rows.append([f"{self.now():.3f}", seg[2], seg[3], seg[4], seg[5], self.fired,
                          f"{speeds[0]:.3f}", f"{speeds[1]:.3f}",
                          *[f"{x:.3f}" for x in travel[0]], int(from_low[0]),
                          *[f"{x:.3f}" for x in travel[1]], int(from_low[1])])
        self.fired = ""

    def on_draw(self, frame):
        if self.t0 is None:
            self.t0 = time.time()
        t = self.now()
        seg = self.segment(t)
        _, end, phase, kind, hand, rep, title, subtitle = seg
        if phase == "go" and self.last_go != (kind, hand, rep):
            self.last_go = (kind, hand, rep)
            beep()
        colour = {"go": (0, 200, 0), "rest": (60, 60, 60), "announce": (160, 90, 0),
                  "ready": (160, 90, 0), "done": (60, 60, 60)}[phase]
        cv2.rectangle(frame, (0, 0), (frame.shape[1], 110), colour, -1)
        cv2.putText(frame, title, (15, 55), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1.4, (255, 255, 255), 3)
        cv2.putText(frame, subtitle[:60], (15, 95), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, (255, 255, 255), 2)
        if phase in ("ready", "announce"):
            cv2.putText(frame, f"{max(0.0, end - t):.0f}", (frame.shape[1] - 90, 70),
                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 2.0, (255, 255, 255), 4)

    def on_frame(self):
        return self.now() >= self.end

    def save(self, folder):
        os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
        path = os.path.join(folder, time.strftime("session_%Y%m%d_%H%M%S.csv"))
        with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
            writer = csv.writer(f)
            writer.writerow(self.COLUMNS)
            writer.writerows(self.rows)
        return path


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--max-seconds", type=float, help="stop early (used for testing the tool)")
    parser.add_argument("--ready-seconds", type=float, default=8.0)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    session = Session(build_timeline(args.ready_seconds), args.max_seconds)
    print(f"Session length about {session.end:.0f} s. Look at the camera window.")
    try:
        pose_tracker.main(on_punch=session.on_punch, on_features=session.on_features,
                          on_draw=session.on_draw, on_frame=session.on_frame)
    finally:
        path = session.save(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "tuning_data"))
        print(f"Saved {len(session.rows)} frames to {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
